An estimation of the $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ decay time for $B^0_s$ mesons has been made with the help of around 37 picobarns of LHCb data from 2010. This measure allows for constraints on theories beyond the Standard Model that may influence the $B^0_s$ system and was found to be 1.440 picoseconds by employing two methods with varying degrees of uncertainty, specifically 0.096 (statistical) ± 0.008 (systematic) ± 0.003 (model-based).

This research paper focuses on the numerical solution of a stochastic control problem governed by a parabolic equation with the control variable affecting the diffusion coefficient, particularly with the presence of rough inputs; it establishes the convergence of a specific numerical discretization method and provides an alternative solution using a stochastic simulation technique known as the Monte-Carlo method.

Our in-depth examination of extremely energetic cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory reveals significant patterns of large-scale anisotropy. At the higher end of our energy range, a specific anisotropy signal was initially reported - namely, a right ascension-based dipolar modulation. To further investigate, we divided the most energetic group into three segments, and discovered that this anisotropy becomes increasingly pronounced with rising energy levels above 4 EeV, exhibiting an energy-dependent pattern that adheres to a power law with an index of 0.77 ± 0.17. We also discovered that the orientation of these anisotropy patterns supports their extragalactic origins, and that on the sky, an anisotropy with quadrupolar characteristics emerges when we compare the most energetic and less energetic energy ranges.

The ATLAS detector at the LHC gathered p+Pb data with a centre of mass energy of 5.02 TeV and 25 nanobarns of integrated luminosity, enabling a comparison with interpolated pp measurements at 2.76 and 7 TeV. Owing to its sophisticated design and reliability, the ATLAS detector successfully collected a comprehensive dataset during heavy ion and proton-proton runs. As a result, it facilitated precise measurements of the nuclear modification factor, obtained by dividing charged particle yields from heavy ion collisions by their proton-proton counterparts in various centrality ranges and rapidity intervals. Furthermore, this analysis revealed a notable variation in the nuclear modification factor with transverse momentum, showing a more pronounced trend in more peripheral collisions.

Quantum mechanics can be explored on noncommutative spaces, characterized by specific commutation relations that define the structure constants of a Lie algebra. By transforming the coordinates into linear differential operators in a commuting momentum space, we can reformulate these commutation relations. This study aims to systematically analyze potential obstructions in achieving a unitary representation of these algebras and devise methods to extract physical parameters from mathematical constructs, including the essential spectrum and scattering indices. As a practical example, we examine a noncommutative harmonic oscillator, compute its essential spectrum, and compare results with existing studies, also discussing the implications for macroscopic harmonic resonators.

In evaluating the potential of federated learning, we tested its performance in training deep learning models to analyze digitized tissue samples, specifically in a classification application involving the detection of tumor cells within whole-slide images. By simulating a FL environment with a large, diverse dataset of cancer images from various sources, we trained models using both traditional centralized and federated learning approaches. Our results indicate that federated learning can produce models with comparable accuracy to those trained through conventional methods, despite never directly accessing the extensive training dataset. This method offers an alternative for developing robust AI systems in areas where assembling large datasets is challenging due to privacy restrictions or data sharing limitations.

In this study, a high-speed optical transmission system is demonstrated, achieving a data rate of 112 Gbit/s (100-Gbit/s wide) using a 50-kilometer underwater single-mode fiber, influenced by macro-bend losses that cause significant burst errors. To mitigate the impact of these errors on the decision-feedback equalizer, an analysis of its error-propagation behavior indicates rapid recovery within 5 to 10 symbol periods following an initial large error burst, in contrast to an exponential recovery period of around 30 symbol periods without the feedback equalizer. A theoretical model has also been developed for the equalizer's response to large error bursts, and its validity confirmed through simulation and real-world testing using an underwater communication link, analyzing the equalizer's residual error-burst length distribution.

Deep Learning models like Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs) hold great promise for handling time-series data. TCNs leverage a technique called time-dilated convolution that poses an optimization challenge which typically demands significant experimentation. We've developed a technique called Pruning In Time (PIT) to simplify TCNs during the training process, allowing for automatic dilation factor optimization. PIT leads to a more streamlined architecture and enhanced model performance, often outperforming manually designed network structures. As a result, we've discovered that ideal dilation sequences often follow non-uniform distribution patterns. Furthermore, our method is versatile and can be applied to various TCN variants and convolution kernel sizes. Notably, PIT has produced some highly efficient dilation sequences, including a set of nine sequential numbers (i.e., 1-1-3-5-7-9-11-15-21) through which we've created an innovative, optimized TCN that exhibits impressive accuracy and inference efficiency.
This paper proves that any finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebra over a given field possesses a specific characteristic - nilpotency, building on a previous discovery that these algebras are solvable.

This study provides first-time data on the fluctuations of a specific angle and magnitude related to a phenomenon observed in high-energy collisions between lead atoms at the LHC, specifically at 5.02 TeV and 8 TeV, with a focus on collisions occurring at the equator of the atoms. Researchers analyzed flow coefficients (v_n) for various harmonics (n = 2, 3, 4) related to the plane of a certain type of particle known as a "s-photon". These analyses were based on a large dataset of collisions, totaling 14.7 trillion cross-section units, acquired by the ALICE detector between September 2015 and November 2015. The results revealed an intrinsic fluctuation in the angle and magnitude of this phenomenon that exceeded what could be attributed to measurement inaccuracies, which had important implications for understanding the underlying physics, particularly in relation to a theoretical model known as the quark-gluon plasma.

The unified correspondence theory leverages the algebraic and order theoretic underpinnings of Sahlqvist correspondence to offer versatile tools for analyzing correspondence within diverse semantic frameworks and logical systems. These tools, specifically root preservation and parameter preservation, enable automatic derivation of first-order correspondents in back-and-forth semantics. Notably, they can be applied irrespective of the semantics employed. However, certain complexities such as non-distributive lattices, infinitely many variables, and conditional rules pose challenges that require tailored investigations. In this research, we focus on extensional and intensional definitions found in anaphoric logic and demonstrate how to compute their first-order correspondents using algebraic corollaries of back-and-forth semantics. Our methodology retains the integrity of the semantic structures inherent in these definitions.

This research focuses on addressing inconsistencies in data tables that contain missing values and functional relationships. Unlike conventional approaches that require adherence to these dependencies, our work aims to explore theories for handling instances that breach certain dependencies, with no preconditions on the presence of missing values. We establish a framework where each data entry can be associated with a truth status: true, false, inconsistent, or undetermined. Furthermore, our framework facilitates examination of pressing problems like data quality assessment, query validity, and data consolidation, leveraging the concept of reachability to determine the data status of composite entries.

This study presents a novel dynamic econometric model called Time-Varying Poisson AutoRegressive with external covariates, specifically designed to analyze and forecast count-based time series data. Our research indicates that a score-driven approach is particularly effective in capturing the evolution of time-varying parameters and allows for modeling complex dynamics and shifts within count-based time series. Furthermore, the TV-PAR model is shown to excel in forecast accuracy when compared to popular and established forecasting methods.

We introduce Neural Descriptor Fields (NDFs), a novel object representation that
replicates both object points and relative descriptors in relation to a fixed world
coordinate system, accounting for the 3D rotation and orientation of individual object
points. Due to its rotation-independence, the representation remains stable in the
presence of object rotation, facilitating the development of invariant task-specific
loss functions for learning tasks. Furthermore, its inherent richness facilitates
training of controllers using only a fixed dataset, regardless of the object's 3D
rotation. Our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of NDFs in task learning
tasks including grasp selection from multiple equally probable options among various
possible rotations of a single object, and object classification and pose prediction
from a dataset with rotations across different views and orientations of a variety of objects.
NDFs also perform better than the recent SO(3)-equivariant representations on the
single-object pose prediction task.

The SiD Detector is one of the two validated detector designs for the future ILC, specifically tailored to meet precision demands for the Higgs boson and other research areas while maintaining an adaptable sensitivity to diverse potential discoveries. The SiD's robust silicon vertex and tracking system, complemented by its high central magnetic field, ensures precise momentum measurement. The detector's finely granulated calorimeter system, designed for particle flow analysis, delivers accurate energy resolution across a wide energy range. Given the approaching construction timeline for the ILC, the time has come to reassess the design choices made during the design phase and incorporate the recent breakthroughs in technology into the review process. This review will discuss R&D prospects and participation opportunities for the SiD's development areas.

We performed the first in-depth examination and measurement of the velocity dispersion and mass spectrum within the globular cluster Tonantzintla 2, located in the inner bulge of the Milky Way. Previous studies had only brief mentions of this cluster. We obtained a comprehensive spectrum for 14 member stars of Tonantzintla 2 using the APOGEE-2 system. These observations enabled us to accurately measure the velocity dispersion of the cluster (0.55 km/s) and confirm its compact spatial profile (0.145 pc). These characteristics, along with the detection of internal gravity forces in the velocity spectrum, indicate that Tonantzintla 2 is a dense, dense, and massive cluster, despite its relatively young age of 3.0 billion years. We also compared the chemical composition of Tonantzintla 2 to that of other clusters in the Milky Way's bulge, and found them to be remarkably similar. We also note that Tonantzintla 2 exhibits internal differentiation in the form of helium enrichment and a mix of sodium and aluminum isotopes within specific regions of the cluster. We also suggest that dynamic interactions and/or stellar evolution may have contributed to this phenomenon. We also explore the possibility of multiple formation mechanisms and suggest that further study of this type of cluster is necessary.

The Isabelle Archive of Formal Proofs has amassed substantial size over recent years, representing an impressive compilation of research and offering a diverse range of opportunities for statistical exploration in the field of theorem proving. Despite the numerous contributions made so far, the ever-expanding nature of the archive still poses challenges: finding specific content has become increasingly difficult, certain proofs lack reusability due to environment complexities, and maintaining the quality of the proofs has emerged as a significant concern. This paper delves into various aspects of the Isabelle Archive by presenting statistical analyses of its content, presenting the findings of original research, and proposing several enhancements to address quality and navigability concerns, including the development of a novel, high-performance search tool now accessible to all users.

Using the functional renormalization group at the next-to-leading order in the derivative expansion, we have updated the position of the Yang-Lee edge singularity for O(N) universality classes in classic scenarios through calculations for multiple values of N, including non-integer N. These calculations utilize a parameter set via a functional beta function and demonstrate that our results are consistent with previous findings from various methodologies. Specifically, we have found the critical positions for various N values: $\xi^{-1}_{cr}$ = 0.130 for N=2, 0.129 for N=1, and previously unreachable high-precision positions of $\xi^{-1}_{cr}$ = 0.128(2) for N=0 and 0.1276(6) for N=-2 for quantum Ising and Potts models in two dimensions.

In statistics and machine learning, it is frequently essential to establish whether a basic optimization method on a non-convex function can eventually enter a region where the function becomes locally convex. To address this, we developed an inequality that enables us to analyze the properties of the optimization landscape surrounding the solutions produced by an approximate message passing (AMP) algorithm. Specifically, we applied our inequality to demonstrate the local convexity of a particular TAP free energy function, which is relevant to the Z2 synchronization problem and the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model. Additionally, our inequality led to a confirmation of a previous conjecture regarding the efficiency of a sampling algorithm in the "easy" regime of these models.

Modern metasurfaces, at the intersection of advanced technology and science,  
constitute an intricate field, involving electromagnetic systems characterized by  
thin, two-dimensional, periodic, and complex geometries.  Current research in this  
area is rapidly progressing across multiple directions, however keeping pace with  
these changes remains a difficult task.  To streamline this process, we present a  
unified computational framework, which is both robust and adaptable to various  
design parameters, enabling a detailed analysis of metasurface behavior across a  
broad frequency spectrum.  As a practical application of this framework, we  
examined the spectral properties of polaritonic metasurfaces, consisting of  
silicon-on-insular rib waveguides, which exhibit an intricate dynamic governed by  
coupled wave dynamics.  Our analysis, which involves a comprehensive  
computational approach, provides in-depth insights into the metasurface's spectral  
landscape, allowing it to explore spatially varying modes, and surface-bound  
modes, and leads to a performance map that characterizes its efficiency under  
specific conditions of excitation.  Our research also reveals the intricate  
dynamic of these modes and exposes a previously unobserved phenomenon of mode  
mixing, resulting in unique localized hotspots, and may facilitate the  
development of innovative components in the fields of photonics and quantum  
optics.  Furthermore, our research opens up avenues for future studies, which  
could involve low-dimensional topological systems, and may unearths

The primary objective of this research is to validate the smooth local orbital linearization theorem for smooth vector fields with a full set of nearby first integrals, especially those at nondegenerate singular points. This theoretical validation relies heavily on key concepts, including the formal orbital linearization theorem for formally integrable vector fields, the application of the blowing-up technique, and the application of the Sternberg-Chen theorem regarding formally equivalent smooth hyperbolic vector fields.

This report outlines a deep learning approach known as the Electron Correlation
Potential Neural Network (eCPNN), which can learn simplified potential functions
that accurately capture the intricate instantaneous relationships among electrons
within complex atomic systems. Trained in an unsupervised manner with constrained
data derived from Full Configuration Interaction one-electron density functions, the
eCPNN model effectively predicts total atomic energies with remarkable precision.

We have serendipitously identified a massive arc-like structure, dubbed a Giant Arc, which lies at a redshift of approximately 0.6 and spans nearly 1 billion light-years across the sky. This discovery was made through a combination of 14 individual galaxy surveys, which when overlaid, revealed the remarkable arc formation. It was discovered to exist within the medium to dense regions of the Sloan Digital Sky Survey, which is filled with numerous examples of the arc. Further analysis using de-projection techniques and size estimations, revealed that the arc formation is not due to observational biases, but rather a genuine phenomenon. However, its existence challenges our current understanding of the large-scale structure of the universe, which is typically modeled using random distribution or power-law techniques. Ultimately, we conclude that the Giant Arc represents one of the most extraordinary and extraordinary structures on the observable universe, which is often compared to the famous Great Wall.

While using photometry from stars to measure the night sky's optical pollution by aerosols and clouds dates back to at least 1961, the CIE color system was originally proposed that same year to standardize human vision-related measurements of visible light contamination. Although initial developments followed, research during the last decade has closely building upon those early findings. This paper provides the recent breakthroughs in ground-based photometric research by analyzing the physical characteristics of aerosols, estimating their scattering of sunlight, and examining their impact on climate change. Although using photometry from stars to achieve these goals cannot replace direct scientific analysis of aerosols completely, it contributes valuable information at a much lower cost and can offer atmospheric scattering data covering a broader range, including heights inaccessible to direct analysis. This research will focus on the necessary conditions to achieve these outcomes, a necessary review of the photometric methods used to analyze aerosols' physical characteristics, and an examination of the link between ground-based photometric research and aerosol-derived radiative changes.

A critical issue in regressing six-degree-of-freedom pose estimation from image templates is the coupled nature of rotation and translation parameters, often obstructing the direct application of translation-oriented methods to rotation variables and vice versa. While the neural projection method achieves excellent results, it still faces difficulties in directly estimating the full six-degree-of-freedom pose due to the complex nature of the projection function, which hampers the convergence of optimization algorithms. In order to overcome these challenges, this work presents two primary innovations: (1) DeepHMap is introduced, an advanced method that separates the regression of rotation and translation parameters by grouping similar projections, thus enabling the direct application of DeepSIFT features to the rotation parameters and the utilization of neural projections for the translation parameters, which yields diverse performance benefits, (2) the work of correspondence learning is re-examined in the context of pose regression to leverage its potential in leveraging appearance cues to support the direct regression approaches, which is incorporated in the proposed method, (3) the results of the proposed method, which is termed DeepHMap++, on the CMU Motion Capture dataset and the Human Pose Repository dataset, which outperform the current state-of-the-art methods, while also requiring less computational time for pose refinement compared to traditional methods.

Peridynamic theories have seen a significant expansion in their application across multiple disciplines, due to their ability to model and track discontinuities within materials without the need for complex mathematical expressions. Bond-based Peridynamics, in particular, has become a widely-used numerical method for simulating the behavior of solids and structures. Despite its popularity, there are concerns regarding its reliability and excessive numerical instability. This paper delves into the fundamentals of Bond-based Peridynamics and conducts a thorough examination of its various stabilisation techniques. Through the use of analytical and numerical methods, multiple issues inherent to the theory are illustrated, revealing its inability to accurately recreate basic mechanical principles and its predisposition to excessive fracture propagation. It is concluded that significant improvements are needed to make Bond-based Peridynamics a more robust and dependable theory.

We present GGLasso, a Python library designed to address challenging Graphical Lasso problems associated with irregularly structured systems, typically encountered in neuroimaging and other fields. Normalized by 10^6, challenge instances are presented in a standard format, allowing for easy comparison and evaluation of algorithms. Following the approach established in the original GGLasso paper, we discuss the algorithmic methods contained in the package, starting with the basic Strongly Convex Graphical Lasso problem and its variations, as well as the General Graphical Lasso problem. Building on the foundational work of Friedman and Yuan, we provide an overview of the cutting plane and cutting sphere algorithms, as well as the related active set algorithm, and the proximal gradient algorithm of Combettes and Worsley. Furthermore, the package's features and capabilities are outlined, including its compatibility with Jupyter notebooks and its availability on PyPI.

Numerous numerical methods for resolving stochastic differential equations in molecular dynamics simulations have been scrutinized and evaluated, particularly in assessing the impact of the configuration on the results, and also in evaluating the efficiency of the solutions. A critical observation made during this analysis is the presence of unnecessary high-frequency components in the noise applied to the equations, which can be configured to fit the stiffness of the molecular system's degrees of freedom, and reducing this component can lead to more efficient simulations. The evaluation of the partition function and the free energy landscape was found to be feasible for this configuration, and preliminary data suggest that this approach yields more accurate outcomes in comparing the configurations of DNA and RNA strands, and in analyzing the folding landscapes of peptides.

Numerical relativity simulations of binary black hole mergers in isolated spacetime have been thoroughly studied. However, many large-scale cosmic structures exist as low-mass particulate matter that influence binary black hole mergers' outcomes and gravitational wave patterns. This paper presents comprehensive 3D general relativativity simulations of binary black hole mergers in spacetime populated with wave dark matter, parameterized by its wavelength. Our simulations cover a range of wavelengths from non-affecting short wavelengths to those significantly affecting the merger's outcome, over 1000 wavelength periods at the smaller black hole's circumference. Our results indicate that binary black hole mergers result in a broader range of final mass patterns across different wavelength ranges, with a distinct pattern of power-law distribution emerging at specific intermediate wavelengths. Furthermore, our simulations reveal that the 3D mass pattern of binary black hole mergers can provide valuable information about the underlying distribution of wave dark matter.

We tackle the persistent issue of exponential stability for a stretched Euler-Bernoulli beam on a star-shaped graph with three equal branches. The outer points where these branches meet are fixed while rotating. The inner point is capable of moving in two ways, with rotational movement resisted by dampers. It has been shown that adding just one damper isn't enough to achieve exponential stability, but a specific damper coefficient can stabilize the system when a second damper is added. This solution is found using the direct method by LaSalle.

Researchers utilized acoustic lenses composed of PMMA to increase the detection area of sensitive devices and improve resolution but discovered these lenses introduced image distortion. This problem was investigated and a new lens material called Stycast 1066, which has similar acoustic properties to human tissue, was proposed as an effective alternative. Two-dimensional models and experimental tests demonstrated that the Stycast 1066 lens significantly improves detector sensitivity and significantly reduces distortion, providing clearer and more accurate images. This new material may offer a practical solution for high-area photoacoustic tomography systems.

Our new method calculates a variation of eigenvector centrality for multi-layered networks that incorporate node importance across different layers. In these networks, defined by separate interconnected graphs without connections between different layers, the value of a node's centrality is determined by the sum of the values of the connected nodes within each specific layer, similar to traditional eigenvector centrality calculations. Unlike standard approaches, our approach takes into account the relationships between different network layers and their respective impact on the centrality values. Unlike current multi-layer eigenvector centrality frameworks that account for inter-layer connections, our approach uses a separate set of equations that can be solved using a hybrid algorithm.

We tackle the issue of non-blind deblurring and demosaicking on noisy raw images using a learning-based approach tailored to handle these images directly, with an innovative new component that simultaneously demosaicks and deblurs them. By building upon an existing demosaicking model and incorporating a newly designed module, we train our system on training data to simultaneously demosaick and deblurring raw images. Our system is also performance-matched to alternative methods involving the simulation of motion mosaicking brushes with encouraging results, outperforming them in benchmark tests on standard datasets.

Recently, we generated the $R$-Poincar\'e algebra using deformed Poisson brackets, 
which effectively replicate the Fock coordinate transformation. This transformation 
corresponds to a de Sitter spacetime. In this study, we formulate the Dirac equation within 
$R$-Minkowski spacetime and establish that it is analogous to the Dirac equation defined 
within the de Sitter spacetime, described by its conformally flat metric. We then propose 
a novel strategy to solve the Dirac equation within the de Sitter spacetime by adopting 
the Schr\"{o}dinger picture.

This study introduces an open source Python framework that utilizes background knowledge and observational data for the purpose of inferring causal relationships. This framework is comprised of the 'cdt' package, which executes a comprehensive causal discovery process to identify the causal interactions and the causal network structure among the variables, drawing from established methodologies including those from 'Bnlearn' and 'Pcalg', in addition to pairwise algorithms like ANM. The framework is available on GitHub under the terms of the permissive MIT License.

This study investigates how spheres interact with water upon impact, specifically the process known as surface seal that occurs as the vessel slows down after initial entry. Unlike previous research, this study focuses on surface seal within moderate speed ranges and broadens the speed spectrum by examining both low-speed and high-speed scenarios. A unique data collection system, comprising multiple high-speed cameras positioned at various angles, was developed to record the surface seal phenomenon. These collections allowed researchers to observe and analyze this process from different perspectives. The high-speed cameras with extended focal lengths provided a specialized means of visualizing the surface seal, which cannot be easily captured with conventional setups. The research was conducted using slow-fall and vertical water jet tests to observe how factors, such as impact speeds and sizes, influenced this process. The surface seal duration was found to initially increase with higher speeds or smaller sizes, then decrease after reaching a certain point. The relationship between the impact velocity, size, and viscosity of the fluid was described through a new formula for moderate speed ranges. The research implications can be found in areas, such as paratrooping, aerial vessel design, and coating applications.

A well-known hypothesis posits that gravity at a quantum level must be devoid of universal symmetries. We studied an array of Type IIB four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ effective field theories to uncover the range of universal symmetries potentially present and then investigated why they are avoided. Generalized $\theta$-terms emerge as crucial elements in these theories. These $\theta$-terms generate nonlinear connections between axion fields and quadratic gauge field strengths which, in order to be consistently applied, necessitate the adoption of nonlinear gauge transformations for the relevant gauge fields. The resulting consistent interactions lead to an irreversible degradation of nearly all potential universal symmetries, including conformal and Poincaré invariance.

Mobile devices running multiple tenant applications simultaneously require strong isolation guarantees to prevent unauthorized access and data leaks. Memory security threats, in particular, can compromise user privacy if not addressed effectively. However, achieving optimal isolation can come with performance and resource costs that need to be managed. A novel approach called TUPHI is introduced, which aims to minimize trust while providing robust security for mobile devices through the use of physically-isolated, single-tenant hardware. TUPHI leverages CPU virtualization to create a flexible and adaptable isolation framework, allowing for the efficient allocation of hardware to applications based on their security needs. Evaluations of the TUPHI framework demonstrate its ability to provide strong memory security, limit the occurrence of information leaks to acceptable levels, and provide efficient hardware allocation through the use of a customized optimization method.

We investigated the challenges of robust reinforcement learning in scenarios where an adaptive adversary intentionally manipulates rewards and transition probabilities. The adversary's influence is confined to no more than an $\epsilon$-fraction of all training episodes. Notably, this attack model surpasses previously considered methods. We established a theoretical limit on efficient robust policy optimization in Markov decision processes with $s$ states, $a$ actions, and an exponential dependence on the inverse of the unavoidable corruption level ($\max\{\epsilon, 1/|s| \}$). Beyond this, we developed a robust variant of the cross-entropy method, enabling policy optimization within a time frame of $O(s^2 a \sqrt{|s|} \log|s| \log(1/\epsilon) \log(1/\delta))$, accounting for confidence intervals and failure probabilities. This comes after optimizing the inevitable corruption term $\max\{\epsilon, 1/|s| \log(1/\epsilon) \}$ .

We uncover an unselectable version of the box game paradox, featuring players making remarkably accurate predictions of unknown real numbers without access to relevant information. Additionally, our analysis confirms the requirement of choice in solving the classic problem and examines alternative configurations of the game.

Our calculations using first-principles methods reveal that cubanite exhibits unusual orbital selectivity, with electrons occupying certain molecular orbitals while being localized in other atomic ones. This phenomenon is exceptionally rare in 3d transition metal compounds, providing a theoretical basis for the experimentally observed lack of charge disproportionation, anomalous Mössbauer spectra, and ferromagnetic coupling between adjacent iron ions.

A burgeoning field in quantum physics, known as multi-phonon physics, is driving research into richer and more complex phenomena, with a focus on the interaction between lattice vibrations, electrons, and light, especially in systems that support dark excitons, which have a significant advantage of extremely long lifetimes. This study reports the discovery of giant Rabi oscillations in systems that emit no light, specifically involving up to four longitudinal phonons and the interaction of dark excitons with light, exhibiting an unprecedentedly wide range of multi-phonon physics with a notable feature - an external magnetic field is not needed, with the advantage of easy system realization and radio-frequency control, with radio-frequency fields enabling precise control and variation of the multi-phonon coupling strength, with notable range from weak to strong regimes, with a system that dark Rabi splitting is a key signature, with an unprecedentedly clear and easy-to-interpret explanation, with a tunable radio-frequency field, with unprecedented ease, especially in terms of efficiency and range, with notable results - an extremely efficient conversion of phonons into light with an unprecedentedly high level of performance - around 10 percent, with an unprecedentedly high level of control and range - from zero to two photons per phonon, with an unprecedentedly high level of control and range - from dark excitons to bright excitons and vice versa, with an unprecedentedly high level of efficiency and performance - around 10 percent, with an unprecedentedly high level of

Our investigation focuses on a 2D electronic lattice from a non-symmorphic wallpaper group.  We're examining a herringbone lattice with two-fold rotational symmetry and translational glide reflections.  By applying a single-site hybridization perturbation within a three-component orbital model, we can accurately pinpoint the location of two types of Dirac points - those found at high-symmetry points and those located elsewhere in the Brillouin zone.  The presence of electrons at the Fermi level generates an instability, leading to a spontaneous formation of this particular lattice structure from a rotator-based state, even without any symmetry-breaking interactions.  As a result, our model demonstrates the spontaneous emergence of massless fermions within a 2D system.  By introducing specific parameters, we can also locate additional exotic phases characterized by flat bands with flat-Majorana modes and flattened bands with charge density waves in a non-degenerate basis.

Quantum states known as single-photon catalyzed coherent states (SPCCSs) can be generated via quantum-optical catalysis using beam splitters or parametric amplifiers. These states occur when a coherent state and a single-photon state interact in two input fields, and a quantum state containing one photon is extracted as a result. We examine the success probabilities associated with different preparation methods and analyze the entanglement and non-classical characteristics of SPCCSs through measures like the Cramer-Robbi entropy and photon statistics. Notably, we demonstrate that QC-catalysis yields states with higher non-classical characteristics than QD-catalysis, and the extent of entanglement in SPCCSs is directly proportional to the intensity of the coherent state used.

In General Relativity using the Newman-Penrose formalism, the use of bivectors plays a key role in identifying the precise solutions to Einstein's field equations. This review focuses on explaining the fundamental principles and detailed calculations of bivectors within the Newman-Penrose formalism, specifically by converting a complex self-dual electromagnetic field from the standard Minkowski space basis to the complex null tetrad basis. As a result, we derive the complex coefficients of the Weyl tensor in the context of Newman-Penrose formalism.

A recent framework combining artificial neural networks and mixed integer linear programming for designing chemical compounds has been built upon to create a new method for polymer inference. This new method incorporates a unique way of depicting polymers using monomers, new descriptors that capture their structure, and employs linear regression in the predictive framework. Computational trials have demonstrated that the proposed approach excels in predicting specific chemical properties in polymers, also successfully modeling compounds composed of up to 50 non-hydrogen atoms within a monomeric structure.

This paper presents a unified approach to addressing certain complex optimization challenges. Problems of control, estimation, and system design can be redefined as optimization problems subject to specific constraints. However, given the infinite dimensionality of these issues, it becomes necessary to employ numerical techniques to approximate a solution. We explore specific methods used in simultaneous direct approaches, specifically the transcription process. Our focus is on collocation and integration-transcendation techniques, using a dual-via positive pressure ventilation case study during the COVID-19 pandemic to demonstrate our approach. Our analysis reveals that optimal air flow patterns can be effectively obtained, and the proposed method is efficient and robust in ventilation treatment.

Identifying tumors in the esophagus from CT scans is a significant challenge in medical image analysis due to variations in patient anatomy and a lack of clear features to distinguish the esophagus and tumors from surrounding areas,邻ading researchers to employ multiple evaluation methods. Precise localization and segmentation of tumors in CT images are vital for accurate diagnosis, surgical planning, and disease monitoring. We studied various segmentation techniques and found that fully-supervised methods, where a deep learning model is trained to directly map images to segmentations, yield the most accurate results. As a optimal strategy, we designed an innovative neural network architecure named Esophageal Segmentation Network (DDAUnet), which integrates attention mechanisms and dilated convolution into a Dense Unet. The attention module enables the network to learn significant features automatically, while dilated convolution enhances the extraction of textual information. The DDAUnet was evaluated on a publicly available esophageal CT dataset, resulting in outstanding performance metrics including 0.5583 Dice Score, 5.8455 Hausdorff Distance, and 93.4446 Gradient Angle.

The challenge of interpreting well logs and navigating drills lies in the diversity of service teams and drilling companies, each utilizing distinct approaches and methods. To address this issue, an innovative ensemble-based method has been developed that leverages the unique knowledge of multiple experts to enhance well log interpretation and provide a comprehensive assessment of uncertainty. This method employs ensemble techniques to model the prior distributions of formation properties, providing a formal and robust assessment of uncertainty that can be incorporated into stochastic models of well planning and navigation. An exemplary application has been demonstrated in the estimation of water cuts and thickness of oil-bearing zones in a horizontal well, where the predicted results from the ensemble model closely align with real-world measurements taken during well logging and navigation. The additional benefit of the ensemble method provides quantifiable uncertainty estimates, in contrast to traditional techniques that provide only point estimates.

Named entity recognition (NER) is a fundamental task in natural language processing and a core extraction technique, extensively used to retrieve text-based information for further analysis. One type of NER, nested NER, focuses on recognizing entities within other entities. Most existing nested NER studies apply linear models, which do not adequately capture the hierarchical nature of nested entities. This work overcomes this limitation by modeling nested entities as an integrated whole and proposing a new parsing algorithm to accurately identify all entities at once. Moreover, to address the lack of corpus-level information in NER, this study introduces features based on corpus statistics, including Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) and Maximum Entogram (ME), to enhance model performance and extract meaningful information from the corpus. Our proposed parsing model, enriched with these features, achieves state-of-the-art results on three standard NER benchmarks without relying on label smoothing, start/end character offsets, or external guides, and can easily be applied to other multi-span entity extraction tasks.

We extend the use of tropical methods to counting in arithmetic problems, such as enumerating objects in higher-dimensional spaces using values from specific mathematical structures, like real numbers or complex numbers with non-zero finite values. In the process, we introduce a new signed counting formula for bitangent lines to plane quartics in space, taking into account specific properties of the lines and the quartics, such as their values in real numbers. This approach utilizes combinatorial data and local counting numbers known as Milnor numbers. As a result, this theory leads to the proof of rationality of the counting numbers and excludes certain configurations. This approach also provides proofs of previous findings in literature and establishes a connection to bitangents over the field of Gaussian integers.

Research into the location detection of mobile nodes within wireless sensor networks is currently ongoing. We develop and test an innovative RSSI-based location finding method suitable for 802.15.4 (ZigBee) networks. To counteract interference between different technologies operating in the same frequency range, we design and execute a new method for calculating the distance between nodes. The aim of this approach is to minimize the average error in location estimation, and when compared to ideal, interference-free results, we have achieved a level of accuracy of less than half a metre using actual hardware.

Multilingual individuals possess a high level of proficiency in two or more languages, enabling effective written and oral communication across multiple languages. When communicating, they may blend languages, also known as code-switching or code-mixing, by switching between different languages within a single utterance. This research explores current NLP developments, constraints, and potential obstacles in tackling five critical issues affecting multilingual communities: crisis management, healthcare, election campaigns, fake news dissemination, and hate speech. To move forward, we outline potential future directions and necessary NLP services to enhance access to technology for language experts and those with limited resources for just one or two languages. Ultimately, to effectively address the needs of these communities, there is a pressing need for comprehensive NLP development across various domains and multiple languages, taking into consideration the complex language combinations used by these individuals.

Human-generated descriptions are commonly used to train and evaluate image description systems, which are typically ranked based on their similarity to these descriptions. This method's reliability hinges on the quality of these descriptions. Since, as demonstrated in Section 2, current datasets are inadequate, I believe we require more precise guidelines balancing visually impaired users' needs and practical description generation feasibility. High-quality reference data could be ideal for system evaluation, yet we should also consider other alternatives.

Tantalum oxide compounds, specifically the Ta$_2$O$_5$ material, have been extensively studied due to their well-known dielectric state. Recent research has been focusing on utilizing the Ta$_2$O$_5$ material as an active medium in nonlinear optical applications, taking advantage of its excellent dielectric properties. However, the nonlinear optical performance of the Ta$_2$O$_5$ material is heavily dependent on its crystal structure, which has been difficult to identify with certainty. Various noncentrosymmetric structures have been theoretically proposed, yet experimental evidence is lacking. To address this issue, researchers conducted a comprehensive search for the most stable Ta$_2$O$_5$ structures using density functional theory, while simultaneously measuring the material's structural stability. To further investigate the potential for nonlinear optical applications, calculations were performed to determine the electronic and optical properties of several low-symmetry Ta$_2$O$_5$ structures, while also determining the maximum possible values for its nonlinear optical response.

Previous studies attributed online misinformation dissemination to personal factors, such as information literacy, and social media's influence. Another hypothesis suggests that geography-based sorting contributes to misinformation spread. This research analyzes Reddit's comments to examine the geographic sort's role in misinformation circulation. Our findings indicate that geographically sorted posts receive fewer false alarms than those in chronological order. In contrast, chronological sorted posts are more likely to be shared on Facebook and have fewer factual inaccuracies when posted in accounts with geographic profiles. This research suggests that online misinformation is also driven by significant non-personal factors, prompting recommendations to reduce its spread.

We introduce a groundbreaking, efficient algorithm that detects unusual events in high-speed information systems. Our method uses a compact data structure that uses very little memory, ensuring the accuracy of our findings without the need for in-depth analysis. By guaranteeing the accuracy of our results, the data structure we developed enables the use of a simple, effective algorithm that identifies suspicious events in real-time. Our algorithm was tested on actual datasets, revealing its ability to accurately pinpoint the onset and end of events, as well as their duration. Our method was also shown to be highly robust, with our algorithm successfully detecting events in noisy datasets. By using a simple data structure, our method can efficiently identify unusual events in high-speed information systems.
