This paper details a specialized apparatus built for use in Aberdeen Tunnel's laboratory in Hong Kong. The laboratory is uniquely situated to study spallation neutrons produced by cosmic-ray muons with 611 meters of water equivalent in depth. The apparatus consists of six layers of horizontal plastic-scintillator detectors that pinpoint the direction and location of incoming muons. Between these layers, a neutron sensor filled with 650 kilograms of liquid scintillator containing a gadolinium dopant significantly enhances detection efficiency of the produced spallation neutrons. Additionally, we discuss the performance characteristics of this apparatus.

Ground-based observations of planetary movements around stars can significantly supplement the planetary discoveries made by the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS). TESS provides nearly continuous data on stellar positions and can detect small internal shifts caused by undetected planets. The TESS-Kirkpatrick Survey (TKS), set to begin in 2020, will utilize a variety of instruments to examine the behavior of stars identified by TESS. Each planetary signal is accompanied by a series of observations, in order to accurately account for any planetary movements. The TKS will also collect data on the rotational speeds, ages, and compositions of stars, as well as the chances of finding "Goldilocks" zones for habitable planets. The TKS will contribute to the development of exoplanet detection methods, planetary population studies, and stellar formation processes. The target selection process for TKS is guided by a set of criteria, which can be represented as a scoring system. The choice of the best stars for observation is determined by several factors, including the likelihood of detecting planets, as well as other scientific goals. The target list for TKS consists of around 6000 stars, and examples of detected exoplanets are provided.

The growth of Information Technology has significantly altered how information is shared, making it necessary to convert printed documents into digital formats.  There has been an increase in fraudulent activities lately, necessitating more effective security measures.  To effectively prevent such activities, verifying an individual's identity through their ID card is crucial, but manually extracting information from multiple ID cards can be both time-consuming and laborious.  To overcome this obstacle, optical character recognition (OCR) has been employed to automate the extraction process, but inaccuracies in (OCR) output can be rectified by (NLP) processing, which enhances extraction efficiency.  As a result, this research proposes a combined approach of (NLP) processing and (OCR) to prevent fraud and ensure more secure transactions.  To test the effectiveness of this approach, three Indonesian ID cards were used, and the results showed that the proposed framework can accurately extract information from these ID cards, with the only inaccuracy being the extraction of marriage dates.  Therefore, this research demonstrates that the proposed framework can be utilized to extract information from Indonesian ID cards, with potential applications in preventing fraudulent activities in the future.

Quantum harmonic oscillators were computationally analyzed in their ground state with either steady-state driving forces varying in intensity or driving forces that changed over time. Calculations of position expectations were carried out for multiple scenarios of mass, angular frequency, and the lambda parameter in both cases. Constant driving led to coherent states, with theoretical predictions closely matched by both simulation approaches. A discrete-time lattice Metropolis algorithm was used to evaluate the imaginary time path integral for these simulations.

The Yarkovsky-O'Keefe-Radzievskii-Paddack effect significantly impacts the rotational states of small asteroids by exerting a net torque resulting from solar radiation reflected and re-emitted by the surface. As a consequence of this phenomenon, the rotation period of these asteroids gradually changes, which can be best measured through light curve analysis. To estimate the YORP acceleration acting on asteroids 1992 SK, Geographos, and Toro, researchers conducted simulations using radiative transfer models that account for the surface properties of these asteroids. The YORP accelerations were found to range from $10^{-8}$ to $10^{-10}~\mathrm{m/s^2}$ for all three asteroids, although the exact values are subject to uncertainty due to the difficulty in accurately measuring the asteroids' surface temperatures. Furthermore, to gain a better understanding of the YORP effect's impact on asteroids, researchers should prioritize the simultaneous observation of multiple asteroids during the same apparition.

The youth are increasingly relying on Instagram to express their political opinions, making the platform's discussion dynamics essential to study. By examining posts and comments from the @BarackObama account over three years, we've identified key aspects of the online discussion network. Our research indicates that conversations on Instagram are often fragmented and characterized by small, loosely connected clusters. Furthermore, we found sound to play a crucial role in motivating users to engage in conversations, as acoustically prominent comments are more likely to be replied to. Our team developed a method to classify comments based on their online discussion network position, and found that comments receiving more replies tend to be deemed more relevant by other users. These findings can serve as a foundation for further investigations into online discussion systems. By understanding what drives users to participate in conversations, we may one day create more effective automated tools to facilitate productive online debates.

We show that any subgroup of homeomorphisms of a compact surface that fix the boundary, whose action within the surface's interior is highly transitive, cannot be topologically compact when using the compact-open topology's inherited structure.

Researchers studied 79 stars with the M-dwarf Ultraviolet Spectroscopic Sample to establish a reliable method for measuring their basic physical properties. By analyzing 102 spectral samples, they found that this methodology accurately reflects the actual properties of M-dwarfs within a margin of 10-15%. They also discovered that the MUSS stellar parameters correlate strongly (r > 0.9) with results from other sources such as M-dwarf fundamental diagrams, M-dwarf distance estimates from Gaia EDR3, and M-dwarf properties from the M-dwarf Fundamental Diagram Sample. Notably, the data indicates that 63% of the MUSS stars have an estimated mass greater than 0.13 M$_{\odot}$ and 41% of the M-dwarfs are likely older than one billion years.

Confining modes to the edge of a waveguide offers the advantage of obtaining a linesource with low loss and a large effective aperture, which can be attained with a significantly smaller physical aperture compared to a point source, this can be achieved by engineering the groove width along the interface between two media with reversed periodic structures, as demonstrated in prior studies, a recent study now shows that the directional line waves generated in this interface can be controlled, an engineered dual metasurface with asymmetric unit cells in each half of the interface can not only confine modes with sub-wavelength widths but also steer these modes into transverse line waves generated in the high-impedance side, this surface can be realized with cross-shaped split-ring resonators, as theoretical analysis and numerical simulations indicate, this dual metasurface exhibits nearly balanced impedance characteristics and near-zero phase variations across its interface, this allows for efficient excitation of directional line waves, this can be verified with a numerical simulation of an optical scenario, this demonstrates that the dual metasurface exhibits high efficiency in generating directional line waves, this surface exhibits high efficiency in generating directional line waves with over ninety percent efficiency, this research opens up opportunities for improving the performance of devices that require optical manipulation of particles and field enhancement in nano-gaps.

Although a key function in database management, query evaluation classification lacks comprehensive guidelines when dealing with self-joined queries. Our investigation aims to bridge this knowledge gap by examining how self-joins impact the complexity of enumerating database results, building on existing research. By extending two known categories of classification to incorporate self-joined queries with respect to efficiency, this study provides an in-depth analysis and illustrates potential enumeration strategies using self-joins. The study introduces new methods to describe query structures and simplifies complexity determination in certain cases. The complexity of case-specific enumeration tasks is classified in relation to underlying query forms in relation to self-join components, and results are proven using structural decomposition of queries. The results indicate that the complexity of enumeration relations can be significantly impacted by self-join components, providing insights into the complexity of enumerating database results with respect to query structure and efficiency.

Multiple formal models can equivalently define functions that map infinite words to other infinite words, including MSO-transducers, certain transductions by deterministic higher-order tree automata, and a specific class of weighted co-B\"{u}chi automata. This study seeks to identify a comprehensive class of such functions that have computable representations using each of these models. For the purpose of this study, representation systems are established for each model and a definition is provided for the executable functions that can be represented by each system. Ultimately, it is demonstrated that the set of functions executable by each system is identical to the class of functions computably representable by MSO-transducers.

Researchers have analyzed collision data with an integrated luminosity of 3 inverse femtobarns, and through amplitude analysis of specific two-body decay events, have discovered that the $B^0$ decay to a pair of $K^*$ mesons exhibits a higher fraction of longitudinal polarization than the $B^0_s$ decay to the same mesons. Furthermore, this difference in longitudinal polarization was utilized to determine the branching fraction of the $B^0$ decay to a pair of $K^*$ mesons.

A machine learning technique known as reservoir computing generates a model that mimics complex systems and can be trained on significantly smaller amounts of data compared to alternative methods. The latest version of this approach simplifies training by minimizing the need to adjust numerous parameters. In a recent experiment involving a highly complex system with distinct time scales and multiple coexisting patterns of behavior, a reservoir computer of the new design demonstrated several advantages over its traditional counterpart. Specifically, it used a much smaller amount of data for training, a much shorter time to adjust its performance, a smaller number of parameters to adjust, and a much higher level of accuracy in predicting patterns of behavior, even when those patterns change rapidly. In addition to this performance, it was able to predict areas of stability accurately, further confirming the benefits of this new algorithm.

A new bias-corrected estimator has been created for the mean absolute deviation of a median regression model, addressing the problem of irregularity that typically hinders conventional bias reduction.  To overcome this limitation, a specific alternative strategy was implemented.  Establishing the bias correction involves verifying the local asymptotic normality property and a specific Bahadur-Kiefer representation.  Developed within the context of a traditional asymptotic framework, this proposal appears useful and adaptable to high-dimensional settings, as well as scenarios involving heavy-tailed distributions and nonlinear dependence.  The effectiveness of the bias-corrected estimator has been verified via simulation.

To address scalability issues with Eulerian methods for robust control and detection in real-time applications, we've developed a variational Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs equation of second-order type to generate smooth, high-quality reachable sets. By integrating a first-order second-order variational form of this equation, we've created an innovative scheme capable of producing both reachable sets and optimal feedback controls. This approach offers efficiency and quality advantages over traditional reachable sets methods, providing a means to combine the strengths of Eulerian and Lagrangian frameworks.

Multi-Layer Perceptrons are widely used for approximating functions due to their periodic activation functions, which are effective for representing periodic functions. However, their performance is limited when dealing with non-periodic functions, as increasing the network's depth to model functions with finite support often leads to performance degradation. This study proposes a novel approach to enhance the periodic activation function's representational capacity without expanding the network's depth. It suggests that periodically activated neurons should be organized into localized clusters to efficiently model functions with finite support. These clusters are expected to be organized in a grid-like pattern, providing the approach with significant theoretical advantages. It demonstrates that this organization allows the approach to accurately model functions with high precision and at a rate of $O\left(\log(1/\epsilon)\right)$ in terms of sample complexity. These results indicate robust generalization capabilities, as theory and results show high sample efficiency across various functions. The approach is supported by an adaptive learning algorithm that requires only minimal hyperparameters. It exhibits efficient sample complexity and strong performance in various functions without the need for extensive training data, as various experiments indicate.

The underlying structure of the brain's animacy categorization, which distinguishes living things from lifeless objects, has been thoroughly investigated through animal experiments but lacks direct evidence from human research. Our study employs ventral temporal cortex analysis, combining data from healthy volunteers and neurosurgical patients, to reveal a distinct, continuous area along the temporal lobe's posterior edge characterized by heightened sensitivity to living things. This region corresponds to where electrophysiological studies have pinpointed the activation of neurons responding to living entities. Our findings indicate that the brain's ventral temporal cortex contains a specific region dedicated to processing information about living things.

The study proves the nonexistence of Landau-Siegel zeros or confirms quantum unique ergodicity for GL_2 Hecke-Maass newforms at a calculable pace, supported by the broader conclusion that Dirichlet L-function zeros exert a force pushing zeros from all other automorphic L-functions off the s=1 axis.

We have adapted the quantum relational Hoare logic originally proposed in (Unruh, POPL 2019) to incorporate "expectations" into preconditions and postconditions, thereby enabling the quantification of pre-/postconditions that reflect the relationship between programs' inputs and outputs when comparing pairs of programs.

The rapid transmission of contagious diseases is frequently intensified by a single high-transmission event, a super-spreader occurrence. This effect should be given considerable consideration in traditional epidemic modeling. A proposed modification to the standard model involves a single high-transmission event at a specific time during the epidemic's course. A variational approach is employed to derive the model's fundamental properties and solve the free boundary problem. Findings scroll ahead indicate that varying the model's parameters for the high-transmission event can lead to optimal results, and these findings are supported by numerical simulations.

Let's consider a complex topological vector space, denoted as X, along with the collection L(X) of continuous linear operators that act on X. This paper seeks to expand the concept of codiskcyclicity, initially developed for a solitary operator within L(X), to a broader context of operator sets defined as $\Gamma\subset L(X).$ Some key results regarding codiskcyclic collections of operators are proven, accompanied by a codiskcyclicity criterion. Furthermore, we demonstrate its practical utility by investigating the codiskcyclicity of C_0-semigroups comprised of operators.

The paper addresses the problem of bias in vector magnetic field maps, particularly in estimating the component perpendicular to the line-of-sight, Bperp. This issue has been identified previously, yet remains under-researched and unresolved. A primary factor contributing to Bperp bias is the use of Inversion Algorithms (IA) that amplify measurement errors, which are generally assumed to be balanced in three components, leading to a preference for using the line-of-sight component as a primary component in most IA. To illustrate this problem, a comprehensive analytical and numerical analysis is performed, including the derivation of a key equation describing the bias as a function of various parameters. A proposed mitigation strategy involves a simple modification to the data analysis process. To evaluate this, multiple algorithms and data sets are used to quantify the bias and test this approach. The results show varying degrees of bias across different algorithms, with a significant reduction achieved using the proposed approach in several instances. Furthermore, this approach is applied to real data sets, including them in a new, publicly available repository containing metadata quantifying the associated bias.

A comprehensive analysis was conducted to measure the radii of 6097 young star clusters in 31 galaxies from the LEGUS survey. The custom analysis pipeline allowed for a large and contiguous sample, giving us the largest one-shape study to date. The distribution of cluster radii appears to peak around 3 parsecs when measured in a way that accounts for all possible sizes. The cluster size distribution is not uniform across galaxies and seems to be influenced by local environmental factors. The radius of clusters is related to their brightness and the density of their surroundings. The cluster radii are also affected by the stellar mass, velocity dispersion, effective photon mean free path, and the distribution of colors within the galaxy. The study found that the cluster radii are the result of a balance between forces that promote growth and forces that limit it. The group of clusters with the smallest radii tends to experience tidal forces from their galaxy, while the largest radii are limited by the physical properties of the cluster itself. The cluster radii are also related to the colors of their stars, as redder clusters tend to have larger radii. The study used the pipeline to analyze the cluster radii in multiple galaxies and compared the results to theoretical models. We present a novel method for calculating the decay of $\eta_c \rightarrow 2\gamma$ using a hadronic molecule state as an intermediate step. By integrating global QCD fits with lattice QCD, we develop a strategy to determine the electomagnetic form factor of the charmonium state from pseudo scalar meson correlation functions. The proposed method provides a direct and precise lattice calculation of the decay width of $\eta_c$, and based on the hadronic molecule model, the resulting width is found to be $32.2_{-2.4}^{+2.6}$ keV. The method is also applicable to the decay of $\eta_b \rightarrow 2\gamma$. The calculated width of $\eta_b \rightarrow 2\gamma$ is found to be $0.84_{-0.08}^{+0.08}$ keV, assuming a two-body hadronic molecule state, and with an uncertainty of $0.08$ keV.

A sign problem encountered in Monte Carlo simulations beyond half-filling can be mitigated by transforming the integration path, but this transformation's effects are unknown in the case of multiple interacting particles. Our study investigates the application of real-valued and complex-valued neural networks to such scenarios. Notably, complex-valued networks demonstrate a significant reduction in the variance of the sign, requiring approximately two orders of magnitude fewer training data points to achieve the same level of precision as real-valued networks. A duality transformation successfully mitigates the variance of the sign achieved by complex-valued networks. In contrast, successful training of real-valued networks without the path deformation implies their training has essentially solved an equivalent problem without the sign problem.

This paper examines the relationship between integers that are y-friable (or y-smooth) and the Dickman function. Given the connection between y-friable and y-smooth integers, our analysis follows previous studies (e.g., Alladi, 1991) to derive the Dickman asymptotic for the count of n-based y-friable integers, denoted as S_n(y). Under specific conditions (y ≤ n and y exp(y/n) → ∞), our theorem matches the Alladi (1991) y-friable asymptotic (n/S_n(y)) ~ ρ(y/n) ~ exp(-y/n) at the core region (y/n ~ 1). Moreover, the relationship between y-friable and y-smooth integers enables us to derive the Dickman asymptotic for the count of n-based y-smooth integers, denoted as S_n(y)) for all y ~ n. Our theorem matches the Donnelly (2017) result for y ~ n).

Given any non-erasing free monoid morphism σ and subshift X, its image subshift Y under σ and the associated complexity functions p_X and p_Y exhibit the following relationship: there exist constants c, d, and C, where p_X scales by a factor of at least c times d, while scaling at most C, in the sufficiently large integers n in N. If σ is recognizable and letter-to-letter, then p_Y and p_X grow at the same rate, whereas if σ is not letter-to-letter, there are instances where p_X and p_Y grow differently. As a result, topological entropy h_X may or may not be preserved under non-erasing morphisms, indicating that defining a topological entropy for free monoids is not feasible. Nevertheless, we can characterize which non-erasing morphisms σ transform sets of positive entropy into sets of positive or zero topological entropy, based on the properties of σ itself and its algebraic complexity over the underlying alphabet. Additionally, our research on complexity under free monoid morphisms yields a novel proof of the stability of entropy for cyclic shifts.

By leveraging previously acquired skills and adapting them to unfamiliar tasks without explicit guidance, humans demonstrate impressive cross-task capabilities.
This study aims to enhance the cross-task generalization ability of massive language models in unsupervised settings, with a focus on models like T0 and FLAN.
We introduce a novel, unsupervised retrieval-augmentation method known as ReCross, which employs unlabeled samples to selectively draw from existing data, fine-tune the model for better performance.
The proposed method seamlessly integrates both high-efficiency and high-capacity components, enabling the use of a relatively small fine-tuning model along with a more powerful base for retrieval augmentation, with particular success demonstrated by the LRM-Copy benchmark that evaluates models' cross-task generalization ability through editing and evaluation metrics.
Our analysis indicates that the ReCross approach significantly enhances the models' unsupervised cross-task generalization performance, with substantial improvements seen in our best results, where the model achieves a substantial boost in performance compared to standard fine-tuning methods.
The proposed method's components contribute differently to performance gains, with our strategy of combining small and large models proving most effective, with the best outcome achieved by both the retrieval-augmentation method and the evaluation results confirming its efficacy, with a notable 22.5 F1-point improvement compared to standard fine-tuning methods.

This research introduces M-arvedu-Kaczmarz-Fast Transpose ICA, an advanced variant of the traditional transpose method for blind source separation. The 'ar' in the algorithm's name is derived from the Armandad matrix, which is K times a transpose of the mixing matrix. When K approaches one, the linearized surface of the aranged matrix resembles the Stiefel manifold, making the algorithm particularly effective for high-dimensional and sparse data sets. The method optimizes the negative Kullback-Liebler divergence by applying the Transpose gradient to the aranged matrix, rather than the original mixing matrix. Theoretical and experimental results illustrate the superiority of the proposed algorithm over existing methods such as Transpose, M-ar-K-Fast, and the conventional ICA using the Bernoulli-Gibbs sampler. Furthermore, an integration of the aranged matrix and the Kullback-Liebler divergence is explored to introduce the M-ar-K-Fast Transpose ICA, an innovative hybrid algorithm. The results indicate a substantial improvement in convergence and efficiency of the proposed method.

This work offers an overview of requirements engineering in the gaming sector.
Existing research studies on this topic have been comprehensively examined.
Key characteristics of the gaming industry were identified and their connections to broader market dynamics discussed.
In addition, several potential areas for further research within this field were briefly highlighted.

Optimizing hyperparameters in the private version of the stochastic gradient descent algorithm is a critical issue due to limited access to private datasets for hyperparameter tuning. The development of algorithms that efficiently find optimal hyperparameters for a favorable balance between privacy and performance within a predetermined search space is, therefore, crucial. In this paper, a generalized framework is established to determine an optimal balance between privacy and performance, and three cost-effective algorithms are developed and evaluated within this framework. The performance of these algorithms in finding an optimal balance for various hyperparameter sets and privacy levels, across multiple datasets and base optimizers, is thoroughly tested. The results highlight the importance of hyperparameter tuning for the private version of the deep learning algorithm and provide valuable insights for its future development.

For a Coxeter system denoted by (W,S), we develop the concept of a boolean complex consisting of involutions within W, mirroring Ragnarsson and Tenner's previous work. By applying discrete Morse theory, we identify the homotopy type of this boolean complex for a significant subset of Coxeter groups, including finite groups, revealing that its homotopy type is equivalent to that of a collection of spheres with dimension |S|-1. Moreover, we derive the Cohen-Macaulay character of this boolean complex, which can be expressed as a sum of elementary symmetric functions times a specific polynomial denoted by the Coxeter polynomial of W. Consequently, we can determine the rank of this boolean complex for the case where the Coxeter group W is not having the property of being finite.

The Euclid satellite, set to launch in 2022, will significantly influence future cosmological research with its Visible and Near Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer instruments. The authors of this study analyzed how correlated readout noise affects in-flight measurements for the NISP detectors and proposed an analytical method for noise covariance matrices. Through experimental data analysis and simulation, a 0.1 D flux measurement bias was discovered at short wavelengths using the NISP Small format detector, which can be mitigated via dark subtraction with readout noise correlation inclusion. The proposed method can also be incorporated into the Euclid's VIS and NISP cosmic shear and BAO analysis for more precise results, particularly with the new 2026 data release based on the NISP small detectors in the future.

We applied an advanced statistical approach to examine the composition of 40,000 stars in the Milky Way disk using a dataset from the APOGEE-2, focusing on elements like manganese, manganese-to-iron ratios, and sodium. Initially, we used a statistical model consisting of two components for each chemical element to represent the population. We found that stars with low metallicity had two distinct groups, separated by approximately one metallicity unit. We observed a linear relationship between metallicity and the abundance of each element within each subgroup, as well as an inverse correlation between metallicity and the slope of each group's distribution. When we created residual plots by removing the metallicity-related components, we were able to identify non-linear patterns, particularly a scatter that decreased with higher metallicity. We believe that these patterns may be caused by the formation of planetary systems. Our findings suggest that a single simple model is not enough to accurately describe the composition of stars with a wide range of metallicities.

The COVID-19 pandemic spread globally in early 2020, causing severe health and economic consequences. One of the primary challenges it posed was that of rumors on social media platforms. These false pieces of information disrupt public order, hinder the government's efforts to control the pandemic, and undermine citizens' trust in official information. As such, understanding the dynamics of rumors on social media platforms during the pandemic became crucial. This paper presents an innovative approach to identifying high-impact rumor accounts by integrating human centrality with the concept of K-core in network theory. A method was developed to quantify the impact of individual accounts in different communities within the social media network, providing a more accurate assessment of their ability to propagate false information. A case study on social media data regarding the pandemic in China validated the effectiveness of this approach, demonstrating its ability to accurately identify top-spreading rumor accounts.

A novel approach to measuring the distance to galaxies has been discovered by examining extragalactic planetary nebulae. By leveraging the relationship between the brightness of the core of these nebulae and the color of light emitted at a specific wavelength, astronomers can estimate the distance to galaxies. In this study, the authors utilized the VLT/4MOST observations of four galaxies within the Fornax cluster to identify and analyze 1050 H$\alpha$ images. By combining these observations with a previously established catalog of 4500 planetary nebulae, the researchers created a new catalog of 850 high-quality objects in each galaxy. By applying the relationship discovered by Da Costa & Tremonti to these new objects, the authors obtained independent estimates of the distance modulus to each galaxy. Additionally, the researchers compiled a comprehensive database of physical properties for their new catalog of planetary nebulae.

Every day, hospitals around the world gather vast amounts of physiological data from their patients, leading to an escalating interest in conducting statistical analyses to provide better medical care. However, traditional methods of processing this data manually are inefficient given its continuous and unending nature. Our research presents an innovative data management solution, called LifeStream, a stream processing engine specifically designed to analyze physiological data in real-time. LifeStream allows for the development of optimized physical plans for stream queries through special optimizations, resulting in efficient, real-time data processing. In benchmark tests, LifeStream has been shown to outperform general-purpose solutions like EventDB and outperform a customized software solution, all while using significantly less CPU resources.

This research paper confirms that certain types of curves, specifically those in higher dimensional space, do not fit the classification of Bertrand curves except in two-dimensional Euclidean space. A new class of curves, called timelike Bertrand-alpha curves, is then defined and characterizations are provided for various subcurves within this category, including timelike constant pre-omega curves in certain types of space.

The choice of loss function for a neural network is widely regarded as a key decision with far-reaching implications, given the numerous loss functions developed to date, making it crucial to carefully select one. Despite its significance, research on the topic often omits explicit justification for loss function selection. We contend that this lack of justification reflects an untested assumption prevalent within the deep learning community. In this research, we investigate how loss function impacts performance in a supervised classification context. Our findings reveal that certain, previously underappreciated loss functions, including the Kullback-Lieber divergence, can yield superior results compared to established methods like cross-entropy.
A stabilizable boundary feedback controller is designed for the Navier-Stokes equations using a linear control scheme with an oblique boundary orientation.

This research aims to advance the understanding of thermomechanical behavior in polymer crystallization. Strain-induced crystallization plays a significant role in polymer mechanical and thermal properties and must be accounted for during production and final product application design. To effectively capture its mechanical and thermal impacts, the proposed model utilizes a unique decomposition approach for the deformation gradient and applies the Coleman--Noll procedure and minimum dissipation potential principle to derive the model. The resulting formulation is absolutely continuous with respect to the deformation gradient, storage supply, and storage modulus, allowing the application of Radjewo's representation theorem to express the model in alternative forms. The theoretical framework is supported by numerical simulations utilizing a backward-Euler scheme, which demonstrates its capability to simulate strain-induced crystallization dynamics.

To analyze the impact of external magnetic fields on doped Bi$_2$Se$_3$ with spin-triplet nematic superconductivity, we calculated its susceptibility. Specifically, we investigated the nematic superconducting gap's response to in-plane and perpendicular magnetic fields, as well as its orbital susceptibility. A key finding was the induction of an antiferromagnetic neutral texture in the Fermi surface pockets via the Lorentz force, leading to enhanced neutral g-factor values and possibly observable in tunneling spectroscopy. A critical aspect of this analysis was the orbital breaking of the superconducting gap by both electron doping and intrinsic warping of the Bi$_2$Se$_3$ surface bands, potentially limiting tunneling measurements of these features.

One significant issue in Imitation Learning (IL) is that obtaining perfect expert demonstrations is a challenging and costly process. In practice, expert feedback can often be ambiguous, especially when feedback is provided in the form of latent actions. Furthermore, a common scenario exists where the learning algorithm is presented with implicit feedback through corrective feedback, for example, when an agent learns to navigate a map and is given feedback about blocked paths. In light of these diverse forms of weak supervision, we investigate a novel problem where an unknown performance metric is given, but feedback can be gathered both from demonstrations and local queries, for a latent action-based unit. To address this problem, we develop a unified framework that allows a agent to utilize this feedback to achieve optimal performance. We develop a meta-algorithm, Unified Attention Learning (UNO), which is capable of adapting to this feedback. Our results demonstrate that UNO is guaranteed to perform at least as well as the best expert demonstration, but also benefits from this feedback by achieving an optimal balance between the two. To better understand this algorithm, we designed two custom tasks where feedback is specific to certain actions, namely whether an action is blocked or not, and whether an action is rewarded or not. In practice, we found that our method can be effectively applied in a real robot navigation scenario.

Continuous phase modulation detection using conventional differential detection techniques is highly resistant to various channel disturbances, such as phase and Doppler shift. Its basic structure makes its implementation uncomplicated, involving the product of a received baseband signal and a time-reversed version of one symbol duration. Nevertheless, it experiences reduced signal-to-noise ratio compared to coherent detection methods. In this research, the optimal delay for filter bank bank raido (FBR) in memory of minimum mean square error (MMSE) detector is determined, specifically for memoryless differential coherent detection and the influence of increased detector memory on delay optimization is also explored. Analytical and computer-generated results indicate that for an MMSE detector, the optimal delay is less than one symbol duration, and extending the number of detector symbols can reduce this optimal delay.

New findings from 1D core-collapse simulations shed new light on the final moments of massive stars just before they collapse, influencing the properties of neutron stars and the rate of chemical evolution in the universe. Researchers used the outcomes of these simulations to create equations describing the equation of state of neutron matter, chemical yields from supernovae based on the collapse of stars without exotic quark matter. Through population synthesis, a link was established between quark matter and mergers of neutron-star black holes that emit gravitational waves. However, this connection relies heavily on the details of neutron-star physics that are still not fully understood. As a result, such events may or may not be found depending on the specific parameters of these merging neutron-star binaries. A previously reported study discovered the relationship between the quantum compressibility of 1+1 dimensional spacetime and its vacuum fluctuations, specifically focusing on thermal fields at finite temperatures. By calculating both quantities for a wide range of balanced, thermal field theories, the research established the quantum compressibility as a direct measure of a field's available empty states. In the process of analysis, a novel formula was derived that connects the vacuum compressibility to the compressibility of thermal matter in its ground state, ultimately verifying this connection numerically.

Current deep learning techniques used to simulate rainfall removal have been successfully tested in controlled laboratory settings.  The next critical step is assessing their effectiveness in real-world scenarios.  To achieve this, a real-data "rain loop" must be created.  Existing protocols for simulated rain removal studies operate in an artificial cycle of adding and then removing rain from images.  However, they are successful due to the use of manually cleaned benchmark images.  Instead of relying on over-engineered experiments that involve generating and then deleting rain from already contaminated images, we propose a new approach called the Clean-loop.  Our proposed method trains generators to simultaneously predict clear images and identify rain elements within contaminated pictures using cross-image and cross-scale connections along with entropy-based regularization techniques that encourage the use of discrete latent codes to represent rain characteristics such as type, intensity, and orientation.  Moreover, our proposed framework demonstrates that models trained using the Clean-loop outperform those using the artificial rain loop by a significant margin of at least 0.5 F-score when evaluated using real contaminated images.  Our proposed method also exhibits Disentangled Image Translation properties where the models excel at accurately predicting contaminated, clear, and identifiable rain elements within a single encoder-decoder network.  Our proposed method is anticipated to establish the gold standard for real-world rain removal studies and may serve as a model for other real-loop scenarios involving other weather phenomena such as snow, fog, smoke, and dust.

A prominent paradigm in reward learning utilizes human feedback via comparative evaluations, but their broader adoption is hindered by the expense and labor intensity of these comparisons. To overcome this limitation, we propose grouping multiple comparisons together and allowing human labelers to mark sub-regions of a condensed state space representation, thereby efficiently leveraging human time. Through data visualization techniques, we create an interactive interface for users to label these regions, thereby effectively fine-tuning the policy to optimal performance with significantly less human time, demonstrated across three distinct Mujoco tasks.

We discuss recent research findings regarding model companions in set theory within the context of ongoing debates in the philosophy of mathematics. Initially, we explore how the concept of model companions is affected by the signature, before specifically examining the dependence of model companions in set theory. Our analysis indicates that the most intrinsic model companions for set theory correspond to $H_{\kappa^+}$ theories, as the infinite cardinal $\kappa$ varies. Furthermore, we highlight that the Continuum problem has a singular solution of $2^{\aleph_0}=\aleph_2$, which aligns with some model companion of enriched set theory containing large cardinal axioms. This model-theoretic framework is justified by a maximality concept reminiscent of Hilbert's axiom of completeness.
This study establishes conditions and proof of existence for a modified Branson-Paneitz equation under Navier boundary conditions on a finite region of n-dimensional Euclidean space.

Evaluating a person's risk of drug abuse is crucial for creating effective prevention strategies. Machine learning techniques can be utilized to develop assessment tools for alcohol and drug consumption risk. A study was conducted to test the capability of such a model based on input from psychological and sociodemographic factors. Data was collected from 1,558 university students in Spain and analyzed using six different evaluation methods. The dataset included information on various demographics, substance use patterns, and impulsivity levels. CatBoost emerged as the top performer among the algorithms, achieving an AUC score of 0.81 in assessing risk. Researchers also explored the influence of specific factors on the results and identified a connection between certain personality traits and substance use risk. Notably, impulsive behavior was found to be a key indicator of reduced consumption risk.

Our proposed dataset, ATOMIC, is an exhaustive collection of everyday commonsense reasoning rules comprising nearly a million text-based descriptions.  These descriptions are paired with three sets of relevant reasoning pairs that rely on inferred information, covering areas such as cause and effect, inhibitory relationships, and analogical reasoning.  As a comprehensive resource for testing and training artificial intelligence systems in text-based inference that draws on real-world knowledge, ATOMIC stands in contrast to data sets that are composed of explicit information.  However, because of its confidentiality nature, it is not readily accessible to researchers until it is released under an open license.

Portfolio optimization is a complex task in finance that involves determining the best investment strategy to achieve optimal returns. Portfolio optimization is among the primary applications explored by investment firms utilizing the HHL algorithm for portfolio optimization on the Navion-60 quantum hardware, which is a 60-qubit quantum computer. In this study, the NISQ-HHL approach is introduced to incorporate first-order noise into the HHL algorithm for an efficient and accurate adaptation to the specific hardware settings of the Navion-60 quantum hardware. When tested on the Navion-60 quantum hardware with a matrix size of 16x16, NISQ-HHL successfully obtained a optimal return portfolio, surpassing the best possible classical return within a 10-minute computation time frame.

To enhance data efficiency of state-of-the-art end-to-end ASR models and enable them to handle a large amount of unpaired text data through multi-modal training, it's essential to address two challenges: synchronizing the sampling rates of speech and language features and ensuring that the learned representations from the encoders are mutually compatible. This paper introduces a novel bidirectional attention mechanism that combines the learning of both modalities effectively. This attention mechanism allows the model to focus on relevant features from both the speech and text data, thereby enabling more effective training of ASR models. A simple yet effective sampling strategy is also proposed to downsample the massive amount of text data extracted by the attention mechanism. This ensures that the model can process unpaired text data efficiently. The proposed method is tested on the Librispeech corpus, and the results show a significant improvement in word error rate (WER) by 3.48% when both the attention mechanism and the sampling strategy are used. This demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method in enhancing speech recognition performance.

This analysis addresses the issue of optimizing cross-sectional area through a specific point within a complex geometric form. To generalize this concept, the study expands the application to multidimensional forms of any dimensionality. The study's findings are illustrated through statistical average cross sections, analyzing the average cross section through random planes within a specific geometric form. A detailed examination of average cross sections is performed within complex shapes, including the intricate structure of a coral.

This paper investigates the long-term behavior of a randomly generated uniform parking distribution of size $n$, denoted as $\pi_n$. We establish that the first $k_n$ positions of $\pi_n$, $\pi_n(1)$ through $\pi_n(k_n)$, are asymptotically independent and identically distributed with a uniform probability distribution over the set $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$ for two different distance metrics. When the number of initial positions $k_n$ grows at a rate slower than $\sqrt{n}$ for the total variation distance and slower than $n$ for the Kolmogorov distance, this asymptotic behavior is shown. This result has significant implications for analyzing the uniform parking function, as demonstrated by the derivation of the expected number of summands in the random composition associated with the uniform parking function.

Measurements of superconducting nanowires, particularly NbN nanowires, indicate the presence of a critical voltage threshold for dc conduction below which coherent quantum phase slips dominate, potentially blocking conduction. The critical voltage of these nanowires is observed to be tunable using an adjacent gate electrode and varies significantly in response to applied voltage, aligning with expected results of quantum interference but exhibiting unanticipated periodic variations. The magnitude of these periodic variations far exceeds predictions based on capacitance alone and presents a discrepancy in understanding this phenomenon, especially after observing sudden period shifts during measurements. The possibility of attributing the behavior to granular Josephson junctions within the nanowires is also considered, offering an alternative explanation for the findings.

The discovery of T-dwarf GJ 229B in 1995 offered initial insight into its composition, yet a detailed analysis with current spectroscopic methods has been lacking, especially concerning its atmospheric puzzle. Conventional fitting methods struggled to accurately explain GJ 229B's spectrum due to heavily interconnected chemical reactions governing its CO-H2O network. This study utilized the advanced likelihood-based APOLLO code for a more precise determination of its temperature, gravity, and the abundances of key elements like C, N, O, and S, leading to the creation of the first accurate, externally consistent atmospheric model for GJ 229B. The results suggest its temperature ranges from 550 to 590 K, its surface gravity from 5.0 to 5.5 log (cgs), and its elemental ratios fall within specific logarithmic scales, all derived from multiple modeling methods and validated by the accuracy of its model's fit to observed spectra in the visible and infrared wavelengths.

Our study offers an explanation of the structural properties of a thermal medium like quark-gluon plasma, using the framework of electron scattering via virtual photons on this medium. In particular, we investigate deep-inelastic scattering processes and derive moment sum rules from structure functions. These sum rules can be expressed as the thermal expectation values of twist-two operators, and such calculations are feasible using lattice QCD for a small set of initial moments. We demonstrate how lattice simulations can determine the minimum virtuality for a photon needed for Bjorken scaling to apply to structure functions. Additionally, we explain the parton model representation of the structure functions within the Bjorken limit and assess its coherence. In line with typical DIS on protons, a kinematic parameter $x$ here corresponds to the longitudinal momentum fraction carried by partons, where the value of $x$ is dictated by the four-momentum transferred by the virtual photon. However, since the quark-gluon plasma does not contain hadronic bound states, there is no final state interaction, and the parton momenta are not uniquely defined. As a result, the distribution function depends on a hadronic scale, and the coherence of the parton picture is established.

Our proposed approach tackles the challenge of novel view video prediction, taking input from multiple viewpoints. Unlike existing research that relies on narrow angle variations, our network can generate videos from significantly wider angles, up to 45 degrees, without the need for prior knowledge. By processing only RGB frames, we've developed a two-component representation, combining local and global features that enables novel view prediction. Our model achieves remarkable results on real-world datasets NTU-RGB+D and CMU Panoptic, surpassing the state-of-the-art in novel view video prediction, demonstrating significant gains in SSIM, PSNR, and FVD scores of 26.1%, 13.6%, and 60% respectively, without the use of prior views.

In this research, inter-orbital coupling was demonstrated using femtosecond laser writing, which enables orthogonal modes in a photonic lattice to couple with each other at different spatial locations. We characterized an asymmetric double-well structure, mapped its propagation dynamics and successfully created a device capable of spatial mode conversion anywhere within a photonic chip. Utilizing higher-order photonic mode phase structure, our experiment showed that a trimer configuration can serve as a $\pi$-beaming device for orbital angular momentum modes. The described approach provides a practical tool for manipulating the distribution of orbital angular momentum and paves the way for the development of advanced photonic applications.

The Ω-baryon, which contains sss quarks and has only been marginally detected in past experiments, has primarily been studied using theoretical methods so far. A study aims to explore this particle's properties utilizing a lattice QCD approach. Calculated mass differences for ground and excited sss states, relative to an ss state, are presented here for various spacings. A calculated result indicating an (3/2,D1710-) excited state mass difference of 0.61(9)(9)(7) GeV, along with a comparison to an experimental data point, demonstrates the value of such calculations in interpreting physical data. This study also presents calculated correlations to aid in the identification of the Ω-baryon in upcoming experiments.

Airborne transmission risk in confined spaces is significant and is influenced by various factors including ventilation, temperature, humidity, surface area, and human activity generating aerosols, with volume seemingly playing a crucial role in ventilation systems.  To better understand this complex interaction, we've examined the spread of SARS-CoV-2 on Boston transit during winter 2021, characterized by close proximity between passengers and driver over extended periods inside enclosed spaces.  By applying a widely-used well-mixed model and historical data on city trips, we created predictions for new infections among riders and found the results to be accurate.  To further refine this approach, we incorporated variables accounting for aerosol generation due to people's breathing, talking, and face mask usage.  We then used the refined model to analyze the risk of infection and discovered that isolated environments, despite having low SARS-CoV-50 values, could still pose a high risk if ventilation systems are inadequate.  We also explored how this type of transmission setting differs from others and identified the conditions under which the spread of the disease among transit riders can be effectively controlled.

Building on cutting-edge experimental projects such as HIBEF at the XFEL, our calculations investigate the birefringent scattering of x-rays when interacting with two combined optical lasers, considering various possible outcomes. To aid in detection, we simulate actual experimental conditions and analyze the origin of polarization asymmetry in x-ray rates, examining detection feasibility from both theoretical and practical perspectives.

This note outlines the algorithm devised by J. M. Eisenlohr and S. L. Farris to
systematically generate all fully transitive polyhedra in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space. Furthermore, this algorithm is employed to construct a novel polyhedron within three-dimensional Euclidean space.

Broadbent and Lord introduced the concept of unclonable encryption, a unique feature in an encryption scheme where an adversary can't produce two encrypted versions of the same original message from a given ciphertext. Our research expands upon this definition, making it more flexible and practical for implementation. We've also investigated various extensions, including scenarios where the encryption scheme isn't perfectly secure, allows for a small amount of information leakage about the original message, or is efficient to execute. Interestingly, we found that secure schemes efficient to execute are possible in the random oracle model but seem impossible to realize without it. Additionally, we discovered that unclonable encryption can be achieved even with classical messages if some quantum one-time tape is provided as key material.

This study confirms that physical layer authentication in mobile communications can be made more secure and efficient by utilizing the unique characteristics of noise signals, bypassing the need for secret keys. The proposed method's correctness is proven both theoretically and practically, utilizing a simulation aligned with the limitations of real-world devices. Furthermore, a procedure is developed to identify and prevent spoofing attempts from malicious users in a noise-based authentication system. Experimental results demonstrate the method's ability to accurately distinguish between genuine devices and simulated entities, as well as between noisy signals and clean signals, all in a fraction of a second.

We utilized the full tight-binding model and random phase approximation to
explore flat-band plasmons in hole-doped twisted bilayer molybdenum disulfide.
Our calculations showed that lattice relaxation influences plasmon behavior,
so our RPA model, which extends the unscreened Coulomb interaction within the
flat-band sector, provides more accurate results. At zero temperature, we
observed sharp plasmon peaks in the imaginary part of the screened potential,
which indicate the existence of embedded rings in these 2D systems. Our findings
also reveal that the ring radius expands with increased hole density,
where the rings intersect the Fermi surface when the hole density reaches 1/4,
resulting in a finite real component of the screened potential. Our theoretical
findings are supported by available experimental data on edge-resolved energy
loss spectroscopy.

This paper expresses the potential function $f$ associated with an almost conformal gradient Ricci soliton on a Sasakian manifold in terms of the scalar field $p$, determining when the potential function is constant, and establishing a link between $f$ and $\lambda$. We also establish a condition for a conformal Ricci soliton to be a gradient Ricci soliton, and provide a characterization of the soliton in terms of its contraction or expansion rate.

Both celestial bodies can experience mass loss due to an expansive outward flow,
often regulated or redirected by magnetic fields that create a surrounding
magnetospheric field. Powerful star winds are generated by the scattering of the
star's radiative force, whereas in smaller stars and our Sun, weaker mass loss is
caused by thermal expansion of the mechanically heated outer layer. This process
can also occur in planets around low-mass stars, resulting in thermal expansion or
mechanical wear on their atmospheres. Magnetospheres in stars arise from wind flow
containment, whereas planetary magnetospheres are shaped by the external wind's
ram pressure. However, in both cases, magnetic reconnection plays a role in
producing high-energy phenomena like X-rays and radio waves.

The Spin-Orbit Proximity Effect (SOPE) has a significant impact on various fundamental research areas and applications in magnetic bilayer systems featuring strong spin-orbit coupling non-magnetic layers. To study this phenomenon, first-principles calculations were employed on a bi/Co multilayer with nine cobalt layers to analyze the electronic and magnetic behavior of cobalt. It was found that electrons from the bi layer transfer to the outer cobalt layers due to SOPE. Notably, the minority 3d-Co bands near the Fermi level acquired an additional splitting, and an unusual non-monotonic behavior was observed in the outer cobalt layers' magnetization. First-order Mott-Jammin rules no longer apply in this system because of the absence of superexchange interactions. Moreover, a non-collinear magnetic state can emerge when the magnetization of the cobalt layers is minimized. It was also found that increased scattering in the bi/Co interface can enhance the spin-mixed character of the bi band and enable the spin-filtered current to flow.

This paper provides approximate solutions to the fractional time-independent Schrödinger equation in $N$-dimensional space for a generalised Mie-type potential, non-intergrable with respect to time, and fractional in dimension. Using the fractional He's iterative method, we obtain solutions for a wide range of potentials, and accuracy is improved by incorporating a generalized parameter within the iteration formula. Accuracy and reliability of the method are demonstrated through detailed analysis and graphical representations, and results are corroborated by comparing exact and fractional solutions, as well as applying the method to previously studied cases.

We analyze how enforcing a neural network's Lipschitz continuity, as it pertains to input sensitivity, affects its performance. In order to investigate this, we developed a straightforward approach to determine the upper bound for a neural network's Lipschitz constant, taking into consideration various $p$-norms commonly used. This approach enables us to frame training a neural network with a limited Lipschitz constant as an optimisation problem that can be resolved via constrained stochastic gradient descent. Through our experiments, we found that models trained using this approach consistently performed better than those using alternative methods of regularisation. We further found that selecting hyperparameters is relatively straightforward and demonstrated the relationship between chosen norms and the resulting model's performance. The benefits of our approach are especially apparent when neural networks are trained on limited datasets.

Sequential neural network models are highly versatile in addressing NLP tasks,
including those involving rich morphology. This work is the first study to
examine the capacity of sequential neural network architectures to learn
agreement patterns in a morphologically rich language, Basque. We developed a
dedicated dataset and evaluated prominent neural models like BiLSTM, CNN, and
transformer-based models on it. The results revealed that while these models
achieved satisfactory performance, they failed to accurately capture the
agreement rules consistently across the dataset. Notably, stronger models did
not always outperform weaker sequential models. Surprisingly, stronger models
could not always leverage the agreement information contained in part of the
data. We utilized the Basque dataset to visualize model attention mechanisms
and performed control experiments to analyze the factors influencing the
models. The visualizations and experimental results led to the conclusion that
neural models struggle to learn agreement patterns in Basque, as they tend to
rely on superficial cues from the data rather than the explicit morphological
information required for accurate prediction.

HD80606b is an extraordinary exoplanet with a highly eccentric orbit around its star. As it moves along this orbit, it experiences extreme and rapid changes in temperature, transitioning from a frozen 49K to a scorching 1614K within a span of 10 hours. This unique behavior provides an unparalleled opportunity to study the effects of temperature on planetary atmospheres. Unfortunately, observing such a planet in action would be challenging with current technology due to the planet's minimal atmospheric emission at 49K. However, the planet's atmosphere undergoes a dramatic expansion as it warms up, potentially amplifying spectral signatures detectable with the James Webb Space Telescope. To optimize the efficiency of such observations, the team utilized the HETDEX 2kDriftKilogram (H2DK) telescope network to make precise measurements of the planet's transit and eclipse timings. The data revealed a 24-second discrepancy in the planet's orbital period, updating it from 15.59 days to 15.62 days. Based on the refined data, the team identified several opportunities for the JWST to observe the planet's atmosphere in action.

Customized digital games successfully encourage motivation in repetitive exercises required for motor rehabilitation. Nevertheless, the underlying structure of these games may be suboptimal for the intended therapeutic outcomes. Our research seeks to develop an effective framework for game design by analyzing the connection between in-game actions and movement patterns that boost patient motivation. We establish a statistical connection between the rewards given in the game and patient movement statistics, then collect data on the causes and effects of movement in multiple rehabilitation sessions. Subsequently, we apply reinforcement learning to identify optimal causes that lead to desired effects, thus forming the foundation for the development of games that effectively motivate patients in rehabilitation processes. To verify the effectiveness of this approach, we created a simplified simulation to represent the respiratory rehabilitation process, from which the optimal strategy derived from reinforcement learning successfully replicates the "zigzag" movement pattern used in the session, and demonstrates the potential to physically achieve this outcome. We contend that the developed methodology can serve as the underlying structure for the design of games employed in rehabilitation processes.

Our research offers a variational approximation, drawing from the Ambrosio-Tortorelli model, to quantify brittle fracture energies in complex, piecewise-rigid structures, applicable to both nonlinear and linearised elasticity frameworks.

We investigate the possibility of lepton-flavour non-universality in certain processes at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). To this end, we focus on Drell-Yan dimuon pair production and calculate precise corrections to this process at the LHC using high-energy collisions of protons. Specifically, we calculate next-to-leading order QCD corrections to this process, taking into account the effects of variable parton distribution functions. As a result, we find significant corrections to the process, varying significantly with the scale at which it is measured. To further investigate, we consider various scenarios for the parameters of a theoretical model and carry out simulations at the parton level to measure the impact of these corrections on certain observables, such as the invariant mass distribution of the produced muon pairs. To accurately compare theoretical predictions with experimental data, we correct for final state radiation using a quark and gluon, ensuring a more precise match between theory and data. To this end, we present a new set of calculations for these corrections and provide detailed analyses of their impact on the muon pair production process at the LHC. To better understand the effects of these corrections, we consider various scenarios for the parameters of a vector leptoquark model and carry out in-depth analyses of their impact on the muon pair production process, specifically at the LHC with a collision energy of 13 TeV. Radiation exposure during positron emission tomography (PET) scans restricts their usage for sensitive groups, such as pregnant women and young individuals requiring frequent imaging. Utilizing lower-dose PET imaging, in conjunction with structural MRI and computed tomography (CT), can make up for reduced signal-to-noise ratios in PET images without compromising diagnostic accuracy. Still, enhancing the quality of synthetic PET images generated from lower-dose PET, CT/MRI inputs faces challenges due to varying noise patterns and the risk of over-smoothing. To tackle these issues, we developed a new approach based on probabilistic latent representations and hierarchical Bayesian frameworks. Our deep generative Bayesian autoencoder model incorporates a marginal likelihood function and employs hierarchical Gaussian processes to capture multi-scale features. This framework enables accurate reconstruction of low-dose PET images by accounting for hidden features, radiation exposure-induced noise, and robustly handling data distributions, thus improving the quality of synthetic PET images from MRI/CT inputs. Experimental results on multiple datasets demonstrate the proposed method's superiority over current state-of-the-art techniques in both quantitative metrics and visual assessments. Additionally, results from few-shot learning scenarios highlight the model's enhanced performance compared to existing methods.

The issue of tailoring news to individuals' interests while respecting their data remains unresolved. Growing worries about over-collected data and its unintended use have motivated our research on balancing personalization and privacy. Our experience creating personalized content platforms that protect users' confidentiality has sparked an investigation into users' attitudes towards these topics. A conducted survey revealed the opinions of various age groups regarding personalization and privacy. In this research, we are sharing our key discoveries with publishers and the community to inform the design and development of next-generation news recommender systems, which should prioritize the human user and achieve a harmonious balance between personalization and privacy.

A linguistic analysis known as centering theory (CT) explains how coherence in conversations relates to structural elements of language. This paper explores the connection between CT and advanced computer-generated language models that mimic human-like dialogue. We developed a basic CT-alignment model and compared its performance against widely-used neural models. Our experiments revealed that more sophisticated machine language systems demonstrate greater sensitivity to CT principles, but also exhibited signs of excessive focus on certain words, or "locality bias". By modifying the basic CT model to make it less rigid, we achieved a more practical balance between coherence and realism in the context of machine language generation.

We have devised three new parameterized algorithms for identifying whether a directed graph can be represented in an upward planar layout. Specifically, we've developed a fixed-parameter algorithm based on the number of source vertices, an XP algorithm based on the graph's treewidth, and a fixed-parameter algorithm based on treedepth parameter. Our novel method involves utilizing parameterized series-division separators to achieve these results.

The rising intricacy of modern adaptable systems demands elevated automation in their configuration process, thus also accelerating development cycles via rapid, automated workflow integration. A novel automated configuration system is introduced, which can be automatically generated from a programming language defined by its own grammar, the core components of which include a statement's outcome, embedded data, and指令执行顺序. Furthermore, the article outlines the architecture of AWACS, which serves as a prototypical example of such a grammar-based programming language, and outlines its development objectives along with a path forward.

This study examines the operator growth phenomenon in Lie-symmetric systems by utilizing concepts from quantum information theory. We specifically analyze Krylov complexity, entanglement properties, and information capacity within SU(1,1) and SU(2) symmetric systems, leveraging two-mode coherent states as a primary tool. These coherent states enable us to explore operator growth patterns and entanglement structures in a systematic manner, ultimately verifying that certain fundamental features emerge across these systems in alignment with the universal operator growth hypothesis. Moreover, our work showcases the value of leveraging Lie symmetry, which streamlines calculations and renders existing approaches like the Lanczos algorithm superfluous, instead allowing us to extract crucial insights through symmetry-based arguments.

Recently, WiFi has become the primary method for locating individuals or objects within buildings, enabling a variety of applications such as indoor navigation and visual identification. This paper presents new algorithms for estimating distances based on WiFi signal readings, with the aim of providing reliable 1D location data that can be used as training data for more advanced 2D and 3D location techniques. Specifically, this research focuses on deriving visible target distances from WiFi data, and validates methods that involve data cleaning, preprocessing, and the use of preprocessing steps like cyclic removal and linear regression, and different classification algorithms. The results demonstrate that combining the use of cleaning, preprocessing, and ensemble methods, particularly with Bayesian Neural Networks, can significantly improve location data accuracy by an average of 10 centimeters compared to the use of alone.

For nearly 60 years, researchers have been searching for signs of extraterrestrial life through SETI initiatives, with a Dyson Sphere as a primary target - an advanced megastructure capable of harnessing a star's energy for an advanced civilization. A study explores whether constructing such a structure around a black hole would be feasible and efficient in powering a civilization. Considering six possible structures, researchers found that a Dyson Cloud - consisting of self-sustaining orbital habitats powered by photovoltaic panels and solar thermal collectors - would provide the best energy supply. A model was created to determine which types of megastructures an advanced civilization might choose to construct, considering factors like energy gain, resource usage, and stability. Interestingly, cloud-like structures emerged as the most commonly chosen, with cloud-Dyson Spheres offering nearly 10^21 Watts of energy - an enormous amount, exceeding our entire energy supply by 15 orders of magnitude. An example was outlined for an Earth-like civilization observing a Supermassive black hole, where constructing a cloud-Dyson Sphere would create an energy supply equivalent to our entire energy system, but would take over a million years to complete. In contrast, creating such a structure using Habitats would require 10 million years. A potential real-world example, located 2900 light-years away in the direction of the constellation Cygnus, has been identified for further investigation - the object named XRFOTSS J192836.

Network-based services are crucial to society, and as technology advances, more crucial services are made available online. Given their significance, monitoring and ensuring that service level agreements are being met is crucial. However, accurately measuring the availability of online services is a complex task. To achieve this, we propose a novel approach that utilizes peer-to-peer technology to identify and alert on service level agreement violations in relation to agreed-upon availability. To validate this approach, we conducted an experiment using a service and client setup, and demonstrated its effectiveness by detecting SVR breaches with high accuracy.

The beam breakup instability poses a challenge for particle accelerators and typically constrains the maximum beam current that can be achieved, especially for energy recovery linacs with multiple passes where a small amount of charge can generate a large beam current. Studies have highlighted the impact of filling patterns and recirculation schemes on beam and RF system interactions in multi-pass energy recovery linacs. This paper delves deeper into this subject by examining how filling patterns influence beam breakup instability and explores opportunities to optimize design for reduced instability effects. The beam RF interaction in a generic two-pass energy recovery linacs will serve as the focus for analysis and modeling in this study.

To determine the parameters for neutrino oscillation, cutting-edge experiments employing long-baseline neutrino detection systems rely heavily on the development of detailed models describing the interactions between neutrinos and atomic nuclei. The intricacy of these models is significant, largely because existing detectors have been incapable of observing final-state neutrons, which constitute a significant portion (approximately half) of the interaction's energy spectrum for neutrinos in the energy range most important for establishing the parameters of neutrino oscillation. The implementation of 3D scintillator detectors capable of providing position-sensitive detection in three dimensions has opened up new possibilities for rectifying this limitation. The active layers of such detectors can also be utilized to track charged particles, enabling the creation of 2D and 3D projections of the event, thereby facilitating a precise measurement of the energy of the recoil proton. The total neutron cross-section with a proton-recoiling detector has been measured, utilizing a high-intensity beam of 50 GeV/c neutrons and a target composed of hydrogen and carbon atoms, resulting in the extraction of the total neutron cross-section as a function of incident neutron energy and relativistic kinematic variable, according to hadronic interaction simulation with the GEANT4 framework. The measurements were found to be in close agreement with the predictions made by the GEANT4 simulation. The findings of this research indicate the potential for utilizing 3D-projection scintillator detectors to significantly enhance the sensitivity of long-baseline neutrino experiments.

In a previous study, experimental adhesive properties of submicron silica particles in cold and moderately warm temperatures were analyzed, mimicking conditions found in young planetary discs surrounding stars. It was determined that cleaning the silica particles in warm temperatures leads to changes in their aggregation behavior, likely due to the evaporation of contaminants. Building on this knowledge, the current research examines how silica particles respond to higher temperatures, up to 120°C, cleaning them in a vacuum before each experiment. However, the experiments revealed that particle aggregation decreases when the temperature rises to 120°C at all measured humidity levels and particle sizes (0.6μm, 1.4μm, and 2.6μm silica particles). Consequently, theoretical models of how particles interact in warm planetary discs need to be revised. The cause of adhesive force reduction in warm temperatures remains unclear and the study proposes two theories: a theoretical model based on changes in fluid surface tension, and the effect of temperature on silicate glass transition temperatures.

Local Fisher Discriminant Analysis (LFDA) is a localized adaptation of the traditional Fisher Discriminant Analysis, widely employed for supervised dimensionality reduction techniques. The LFDA R package allows users to execute various LFDA methodologies like Kernel Local Fisher Discriminant Analysis and Semi-Supervised Local Fisher Discriminant Analysis. The package also facilitates dimensionality reduction result visualization, utilizing 3D (rgl) and 2D (ggfortify in ggplot2) graphical tools.

Imitation learning has emerged as a key approach for robot skill learning from human demonstrations, which can be viewed as a form of constrained optimization. In this paper, we extend the existing work on imitation learning with linear constraints to include additional practical considerations. We address the challenge of adapting to novel situations, such as different robot starting positions, and incorporate the ability to avoid obstacles in conjunction with nonlinear constraints. Additionally, we examine the impact of hard constraints on convergence properties and present an efficient solution method utilizing constrained Lagrangian relaxation. Imitation learning can be seen as a constrained optimization problem, and our approach leverages this structure to reduce the problem to one with fewer constraints, thus reducing computational complexity. Imitation learning with linear constraints has proven effective in various applications, but real-world scenarios often involve additional complexities, such as obstacle avoidance and adaptation to novel situations.
