We have developed a comprehensive model that enables simulation of the measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution (MDI-QKD) process. It can predict real-world observations and outcomes in scenarios involving linear channel loss, including the associated gain levels, error rates in different measurement bases, and final key rates. Our model is versatile and can be applied to various MDI-QKD implementations that employ convex source states or diverse coding techniques. As such, it is an invaluable resource for analyzing and evaluating the performance of different MDI-QKD protocols.

Researchers investigate polynomial-time approximation schemes (PTAS) for solving specific constraint satisfaction problems, such as Maximum Independent Set or Minimum Vertex Cover on graph classes with limited connectivity. This work establishes a new approach to develop a PTAS for any sparse, non-binary CSP that has a PTAS when restricted to binary constraints, using a combination of fractional relaxation and Brute Force methods. This technique leads to PTAS solutions for specific sparse CSPs, such as colouring and colouring list CSPs, and provides PTAS approximations for certain 3-colouring lists on three-factors.

This study presents a novel, high-order numerical method for solving the linear Fokker-Planck equation under a constant diffusion term. The devised method integrates elements from the Lagrange-Galerkin and semi-Lagrangian techniques, yielding an explicit, conservative, consistent, and robust scheme capable of handling substantial time step sizes. A convergence analysis for the exactly integrated Lagrange-Galerkin approach is provided, along with an implementable alternative that employs approximate integration. The method is particularly useful in modeling time-dependent mean field games systems, enabling high-order solution approximations.

Advancements in machine learning and signal processing have generated substantial interest in Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), which excel at solving complex, engineering-driven problems. Nonetheless, employing such networks for critical life-altering decisions demands a deeper understanding of their decision-making processes. Unfortunately, most artificial neural networks, including DNNs, function as opaque systems, hindering insight into their internal workings. Although some research has initiated the quest to illuminate their behavior, the field of explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) remains underdeveloped. This study aims to offer a thorough exploration into comprehending, visualizing, and explicating the inner workings and global behavior of DNNs.

This study examines a group of rapid rotators known as Am stars with unusually high spins for their age. Evidence suggests that a compact companion, possibly damaged due to engulftment, could be responsible for transferring angular momentum to these stars. This hypothesis is supported by observations showing that these Am stars are more likely to be metallic and tend to appear in binary star systems. Furthermore, evidence suggests that they are concentrated in the galactic disk and core regions. Nonetheless, research using gaia data also reveals that young Population I stars on the red giant branch with high spins are present without a close companion. This indicates that unknown angular momentum transport mechanisms may also be at play in this scenario.

Fake news has become a pressing concern on social media platforms due to its rapid dissemination and potential to cause harm. Although machine learning models have been successful in detecting false information, they often rely on identifying it manually, leaving a significant portion of complex, manipulated content undetected. Such content is common in political campaigns and other high-stakes events, where false information is often created by combining numerous pieces of authentic data across multiple modalities. To address this challenge, a simple neural process meta-model has been proposed to learn the implicit generative model of multi-modal fake news. This model is capable of detecting the existence of such news and, in turn, assisting traditional classifiers in identifying it. Evaluations on political Facebook posts have shown that this detector outperforms the baseline, achieving notable improvements in detecting sophisticated, multi-modal false information.

This paper investigates the age of information (AoI) in a discrete-time status updating system that employs the Ber/G/1/1 queue. We demonstrate that utilizing a two-dimensional state vector which simultaneously tracks AoI and queue departure opportunities can generate the same joint stationary distribution as directly modeling the joint evolution of AoI and queue departure opportunities. We formulate the joint stationary distribution and present an efficient computation algorithm utilizing generating functions to accelerate computation. Experimental results show our algorithm is at least an order of magnitude faster than direct computation, with minimal difference in accuracy.

This work delves into various quantum algebras that arise from a special type of set-theoretic solution to the Yang-Baxter equation and their 'q-analogue' counterparts, also providing common characteristics that these algebras share in terms of quasi-bialgebras and twists. By establishing that set-theoretic and q-analogue solutions produce the same specific types of algebras and by identifying additional constraints for their 'q-deformed' counterparts, this research greatly expands our current understanding of set-theoretic solutions and their quantum equivalents, revealing new general patterns in the field.

Recently, Golay complementary matrices have gained popularity due to their utility in omnidirectional precoding techniques. This research extends Golay complementary matrices to higher-dimensional spaces known as multi-dimensional Golay complementary arrays and presents novel construction methods for pairs and quadruples of GCA. A set of ring identities is introduced to facilitate these constructions. Specifically, it is shown that GCA pairs are possible in four-dimensional space if certain conditions are met concerning the sizes and their factorization properties. Additionally, in this study, we examine potential GCA quadruples in four-dimensional space and provide a method for constructing GCA quadruples in such space, which may have potential applications in polyphase precoding research.

Quantum tunneling in silicon materials is influenced by the valley degree of freedom in the electronic wavefunction, which can lead to unique phenomena not observed in other systems. The valley interference effect arises due to the difference in effective mass between electrons in different valley pairs, resulting in unusual current patterns that vary with crystal orientation. The exchange interaction between adjacent silicon atoms is exchange rate is governed by the overlap of their electron wavefunctions across different valleys, causing a decrease in exchange strength as the bonding direction shifts toward perpendicular. The reduced exchange has an unintended consequence on the operation of memory devices, limiting their readout speed and increasing power consumption. The proposed study provides theoretical models and first-principles calculations to explain these effects, providing valuable insights for the design and optimization of silicon-based devices at the atomic level.

Complex systems consisting of multiple interacting components are found throughout nature, however their underlying structure and dynamic behavior are often unclear. Although recent studies have employed various methods to analyze these systems, successfully applying them simultaneously remains difficult. We present an original, adaptable graph neural network model that can examine the structure and dynamic interactions within a given system from observational data. This framework is applied to investigate the structure and dynamic of two graph datasets and provide novel insights on the circulation patterns within the A380 aircraft's fuel system.

We introduce an infinite family of recursive formulas for calculating the counts of binary integer partitions that fulfill specific divisibility criteria, establishing relationships among these counts via cumulative sums. These formulas have a meaningful interpretation within the framework of graded polynomial rings and enable us to derive computations related to homology modules in the context of stable homotopy theory, utilizing the properties of the mod $2$ Steenrod algebra.

A cutting-edge, minimally invasive therapy called Laser Interstitial Thermal Therapy (LITT) treats seizures caused by intractable epilepsy, and accurate and quick assessment of thermal damage from LITT is crucial for patient safety and optimal therapy results. In this study, an encoding-based approach is devised to rapidly generate thermal damage maps based on pre-LITT brain scans. Initially, we enhance the capability of pixel-based methods to incorporate spatial information into image encoding. Next, we introduce a novel technique called Progressive Adversarial Variational Auto-Encoder (PAVE) that combines elements of statistical learning and therapy knowledge. The experimental outcomes show that our method accurately encodes thermal damage maps while reducing assessment time to less than two seconds, making it suitable for real-time use during LITT treatment.

Strong nonlocality, a phenomenon where systems demonstrate nonlocality without entanglement in all possible measurements, has been experimentally verified for various states representing more than one basis. In this work, we theoretically demonstrate strong quantum nonlocality for unextendible product bases, specifically $LU$-irreducible UBs, in unextendible product states.

The speed at which massive spectroscopic surveys collect data directly corresponds to the number of optical fibers used in each observation. This paper assesses the effectiveness and efficiency of a method to coordinate astrobots in the SDSS-V by running numerous simulated and real-world tests. These trials evaluate the algorithm's performance under various conditions, including a vast portion of the SDSS-V's coordinate space.

GP 2 is a graph-based language that maintains compatibility with the existing GP 1 compiler, which can efficiently utilize older, GP 1 specific hardware. The existing compiler is highly optimized but complex, making GP 2 programs difficult to compile. A new basic compiler version has been created to facilitate the easy compilation of GP 2, offering lower-level features in a subsequent release to restore the high optimization levels of the original compiler.

Dimensionality reduction in high-dimensional data is effectively managed by a technique called feature extraction. Self-supervised learning's prominent method, contrastive learning, has gained considerable interest recently. A new, all-encompassing framework is now proposed to incorporate contrastive learning for feature extraction, which is characterized by four primary components: contrastive learning methodology, data dimensionality reduction technique, contrastive loss function, and framework-specific optimization. Notable applications and a comprehensive numerical analysis are provided after presenting the key aspects of the proposed framework, including its design considerations, contrastive learning principles, data dimensionality reduction techniques, and embedding space optimization. A detailed examination of the framework's components is provided, including the composition of contrastive learning data pairs, contrastive learning methods, and the comparison of different dimensionality reduction techniques, such as PCA and linear regression, as well as various contrastive loss functions, such as binary cross-entropy and contrastive negative mean squared error, leading to the development of a set of rules for selecting the most suitable loss function and dimensionality reduction technique based on specific criteria, ultimately resulting in a set of examples that illustrate the framework's effectiveness and efficiency, including its ability to perform feature extraction for both image and text data, as well as its superiority over other prominent methods, leading to a comprehensive examination of the framework's performance and efficiency through a detailed numerical analysis, including its robustness to varying optimization parameters and its ability to produce high-quality features that are difficult to distinguish from manual features,

We establish an infinite sequence of locally arc-transitive graphs characterized by a unique property: their automorphism groups partition vertices into two distinct orbits while exhibiting quasiprimativity on just one orbit, specifically within a class of twisted wreath structures. Our findings expand upon a framework initially proposed by Giudici, Li, and Praeger by providing an infinite number of examples classified under the star normal quotient twisted wreath category for locally arc-transitive graphs.

Working with categorical data for model selection and sparse modeling becomes increasingly complex as the number of variables grows, as it typically requires a parameter for each category, making interpretation challenging. Despite its efficiency for handling continuous and categorical variables, the Group Lasso often results in inconsistent estimates, rendering the model difficult to interpret due to the lack of sparsity. To achieve a sparse solution using the Group Lasso, we propose a two-step method: first reducing data dimensionality through the Group Lasso, and then employing an information criterion on a subset of selected clusters to derive a sparse model with enhanced interpretability. We validate the effectiveness of this method through numerical experiments and an application to the 2010 Canadian Census dataset.

Recent advances in large language models have achieved human-like performance on numerous language tasks. However, the potential for these LLMs to effectively utilize structured information within familiar domains, such as biology, has been underexplored. We have developed a technique called SKILL (Structured Knowledge Infusion for LLMs) to enable LLMs to leverage graph-based knowledge representations through a process of attention allocation and virtual operation formulation. We have conducted comprehensive evaluations of LLMs with and without the application of SKILL across multiple domains, including general purposes and biology, as well as assessments of potential negative effects on performance. Our results indicate that LLMs infused with external knowledge through SKILL demonstrate significant enhancements in LLM performance.

This article examines spatially nonlocal diffusion models, with a focus on how their interaction range $\delta$ influences their behavior. By analyzing the models' formal limits as interaction ranges either become very small or very large, we investigate their consistent local and nonlocal limits. Our study reveals the precise scaling of kernel functions required for nonlocal models to converge to classical local diffusion models with large interaction scales. These requirements are practically difficult to achieve and raise questions about the realistic applicability of nonlocal models featuring widely spread interaction scales.

When capturing panoramic scenes, individuals often take photos while changing their posture and bending over. Research has demonstrated that keeping cameras aligned with gravity allows for accurate relative orientations without the need for intrinsic calibration. Previously, researchers utilized the fact that people's bodies generally stay upright to solve panoramic alignment problems consisting of multiple overlaps. In this work, we utilize both pieces of information to develop new methods for creating panoramic images from photos taken with front-facing cameras. Given the assumption that images exist on a real-world plane, our approach formulates the problem of determining relative camera angles, given the constraints of gravity and the fact that images lie on a plane. This leads to a set of nonlinear equations representing the possible solutions. By analyzing these solutions in relation to the orientation of the first camera and the orientation of the cameras' up vectors, we can identify the minimal solutions. Ultimately, we employ optimization techniques to find the most efficient set of camera orientations, leveraging the initial camera's absolute orientation. For cases involving night scenes with abundant light sources, we propose an alternative approach using graph optimization to simultaneously solve for the camera orientations and relative depths, minimizing a cost function that accounts for the physical properties of cameras and images. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of these approaches in processing images and providing accurate camera orientations with reduced errors compared to existing methods.

Hanzer and Muić's work on degenerate Eisenstein series cancellations has been built upon, 
extending their method and outcome to a specific set of Eisenstein series, 
specifically those formed from the combinations of two Speh representations 
$\Delta(\tau,m)|\cdot|^{s_1}\otimes\Delta(\tau,n)|\cdot|^{s_2}$ in $GL(m+n,\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$ for self-dual cuspidal automorphic representation $\tau$.

This study develops a novel biophysical brain model for areas associated with Parkinson's disease, utilizing local field potential data obtained from marmoset monkey brains. Parkinson's disease, a neurodegenerative disorder caused by the death of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra, disrupts normal basal ganglia-thalamus-cortex function. Despite its well-known pathophysiology, a computational model that accurately replicates marmoset brain activity in Parkinson's disease states has not yet been achieved. We utilized electroencephalography and local field potential data to compare healthy and Parkinson's disease brain activity, and administered apomorphine to induce Parkinson's disease-like symptoms in marmoset monkeys. By comparing network characteristics, we identified significant differences in the brains of healthy and Parkinson's disease monkeys, and found that the latter exhibited impaired information processing due to altered brain connectivity. We constructed and fine-tuned a computational model that matched the activity patterns of marmoset brains in both healthy and Parkinson's disease states, and found that it could process information less efficiently than a healthy marmoset brain. This study represents a critical step toward the development of accurate brain models that incorporate the activity patterns of non-human primates in Parkinson's disease states, which could potentially inform the creation of more realistic models of the human brain in this state.

Achieving a seamless visual experience and optimal system performance when displaying line joins on vector maps requires an efficient anti-aliasing technique. However, the limitations of OpenGL API hinder optimal rendering results when approximating the anti-aliased effect through multiple triangles. In an attempt to rectify this issue, this study introduces a straightforward yet high-performance algorithm utilizing two triangles to replicate fan-shaped line joins via alpha operation. Our findings indicate this technique yields a genuine anti-aliasing effect while reducing memory consumption, raising frame rates, and preventing overlap rendering in map visualization. Our novel anti-aliasing method has been applied in notable applications such as Tencent Mobile Maps and Tencent Automotive Maps.

Our team utilized the KOOLS-IFU on Seimei Telescope to observe nine GoALS sample galaxies with high luminosity in the infrared, located less than 0.04 in redshift. In redshift less than 0.04, the telescope's spatial and spectral resolutions made it possible to accurately measure radial velocities via the absorption lines of sodium in the blue spectrum. The samples in redshift less than 0.04 were all interactions or self-sufficient galaxies. The spectra showed a wide array of ionized gas lines from [OIII] at 5007A to H$\beta$ at 4861A, with [OIII] being the most prominent. The line ratios in the optical spectrum were plotted on a BPT diagram and were comparable to other Seimei Telescope data in the GOALS sample. The line ratios in galaxies with strong [OIII] were similar whether they were interacting or not. The data showed that interacting galaxies with strong [OIII] had more gas that was ionized. The line ratios in KOOLS-IFU samples with strong [NII] at 6548A were plotted and were ionized with medium ionization. The galaxies with strong [NII] were mostly not interacting. The data showed that interacting galaxies with strong [OIII] had more gas that was ionized. The data showed that interacting galaxies with strong [H$\beta$] had more gas that was ion

The multivariate interpolation operator is traditionally constructed using piecewise linear functions to approximate absolute differences between values. In this study, we develop a novel, transcendental interpolation function derived from the hyperbolic tangent, providing more precise approximations of functions that increase linearly with the distance. Building on the Wu and Zhang quasi-interpolation formula, which employs a threshold function, we adapt our new interpolation function to create a corresponding quasi-interpolation operator. This adaptation enables the preservation of certain functions' convexity and concavity properties and facilitates smoother interpolation results with $C^1$ differentiability. Furthermore, direct interpolation convergence at an order of $O(h^2)$ is theoretically proved. An example illustration is also included to demonstrate the method's practical applications.

Transportation systems are highly vulnerable to weather conditions that pose safety risks and can disrupt operations. To ensure efficient planning and execution of transportation projects, accurate weather prediction from road images is essential. While the task of weather classification seems straightforward, the complexity of weather patterns and variations in lighting make it a challenging problem. To address this issue, we have compiled the largest dataset for weather classification to date, encompassing eight distinct weather categories. The new dataset, known as EDW, contains over 30,000 images covering fog, snow, rain, and clear weather conditions. The characteristics of the EDW dataset present unique challenges for the weather classification task, requiring innovative solutions. In this study, we evaluated several convolutional neural network algorithms using data augmentation techniques to mitigate the challenges posed by the EDW dataset. The results of our experiments provide a comprehensive guide for researchers working on multi-class image classification tasks in complex weather conditions.

To improve modeling long sequences in the time domain for speech separation, a dual-path RNN was previously proposed. While this design effectively handled long sequences, it resulted in excessive computation due to the use of RNNs. A single-channel speech separation model based on this dual-path architecture was developed, but required fine-tuning to accommodate the single input constraint. A novel network was then proposed that adopted a dual-path design but utilized convolutional units in place of RNN units, allowing it to process single-channel input without additional training. Comparative results showed that this new network outperformed both its single-path and eight-layer convolution RNN counterparts in various metrics.

A new statistics technique has been developed using the outer densities of galactic clusters to investigate dark energy and neutrino mass effects on the halo structure. Traditionally, researchers analyze halo profiles by focusing on their central regions modified by past mergers and violent processes. Instead, this study examines the turn-around radii where the expansion of the universe overcomes gravitational collapse to form dark matter halos. Observational data from 29 galactic clusters has been used to derive the equation of state parameter ($\omega$)$ and neutrino mass ($\nu$)$ by comparing cosmological simulations to the observed data. Key simulations considered various combinations of the universe's density ($\Omega_m$)$ and neutrino mass, allowing for a detailed analysis of how these factors influence the turn-around radius to virial radius ratio. Notably, massive neutrinos have a more significant effect on halo structure than a universe with or without dark energy.

Recently introduced multi-fluid models hold promise in refining the simulation of atmospheric convection within weather and climate simulations. A dynamic framework that accounts for fluid motion at sub-grid scales has the potential to reduce the reliance on overly utilized parameterizations of convection. Before implementing multi-fluid models in weather and climate models, researchers need to evaluate single-column models that incorporate this fluid interaction under various Rayleigh-Benard convection conditions. These models feature rising and sinking bubbles of differing temperatures within rising and sinking plumes, all influenced by diffusion and the rate of cooling at the boundaries. We developed and evaluated nine single-column models based on mixing-length theory, assessing their ability to replicate the characteristics of convection under various conditions and their alignment with observations and numerical simulations. Some of these models were further subjected to periodic box simulations to assess their k-e closures and comparisons with observations, finding that two of the models accurately replicated the characteristics of convection, notably the temperature fluctuations, spectral characteristics, and efficiency of convection.

We investigate three separate Jaynes-Cummings systems, with two of the systems having correlated atoms, but the third system is unconnected. Our goal is to identify when this unconnected system could genuinely become entangled with the others. Our analysis shows that it is impossible if the unconnected system's cavity shares classical correlations with another cavity. The unconnected system's state remains strictly mixed, with its entropy never dropping below 1, given that it is possible to separate the connected systems into independent parts. If the two connected cavities are entangled, the unconnected system can be part of a genuinely tripartite entangled whole, provided certain criteria are met. Interestingly, the unconnected system can also be unconnected from two parts while being genuinely entangled with the third. Finally, we show that an unconnected qutrit can be genuinely entangled with two parts via a mechanism called steering.

The Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS) is one of the primary detectors in the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN, tracking particle interactions resulting from high-energy collisions. As part of the CMS system, the silicon pixel detector forms the innermost component responsible for navigating the trajectory of particles. Although initially operational between 2009 and 2016, it has been replaced with an upgraded variant in 2016 to better adapt to increasingly energetic and dense data produced during collisions. This new upgraded detector is now operating and is expected to withstand the intense data output projected for future operations in LHC Run 3 and beyond. This new upgraded detector is now composed of three distinct upgrade phases, with Phase-1 being the primary and most critical component. This paper delves into the reconstruction of data recorded in the pilot blades of the Phase-1 pixel detector, with a specific focus on data collected during Run 2 and processed during Run 2 and Run 3.

A method is presented for computing the Kall\'en-Lehmann spectral density from lattice QCD data, which is initially general for any gauge theory correlation function. The approach for extracting the spectral density's parameters from QCD data will be discussed. The procedure will then be applied to the SU(2) glueball spectrum, where the parameters are derived from Glueball form factor data. The resulting spectrum matches theoretical and other numerical predictions for the ground and first excited state glueballs within the desired precision. The success of the fit for the first few excited states will be discussed. The approach's success and the potential for applying it to hadron form factors and spectroscopy will be discussed.

Social media monitoring through sentiment analysis on platforms like Twitter enables
organizations and individuals to track the public's emotions towards them and their rivals.
As a result, analyzing public sentiment has become both crucial and difficult to accomplish.
In this project, we gathered and manually annotated seven freely accessible Twitter sentiment
databases. We then compiled a new set of training and testing data from these sources. An
LSTM-based classification model was developed to determine the sentiment expressed in
individual tweets. The model's performance was assessed using the newly created dataset.

A linear screening rule has been established for the charge of a black hole on a screen located at the surface of an enclosing shell, with the screened charge increasing with the charge of a non-linear charged black hole in an anti-de Sitter space. Although a perfect heat engine functionality and a universal scaling law for the charge ratio exist under linearity, the non-linear relationship between the charge ratio and the horizon-to-screen radius ratio varies depending on the radius ratio of the screen and horizon, although it remains consistent where the screen and horizon radius ratios are in an odd integer power relationship.

Reconstructing a quantum state of continuous-variable systems like the radiation field is complicated, mainly due to the high dimensionality of its Hilbert space. Multiple approaches have been proposed for state reconstruction, including conventional methods and machine learning applications, yet there's no universally effective protocol for deriving the Wigner function from an optical tomogram of an arbitrary light state. We demonstrate that specific non-classical effects such as the generation of entanglement and onset of quantum synchronization are directly reflected in distinct patterns of optical tomograms, eliminating the need for full state reconstruction in these instances.

Recent advances in open-domain dialogue models have achieved significant breakthroughs.
Despite this, developing a scalable chat system that meets role-specific requirements remains a challenge due to the complexity of defining and achieving the desired role.
To tackle this challenge, we present a new role-defined open-domain dialogue dataset, built by collecting user conversations that naturally impose a specific purpose on service providers.
We then propose a method to train a chum bot that adheres to the specified role, leveraging the scale of open-domain data.
Our experiments show that our role specification is meaningful and that our method outperforms baseline systems on our constructed testing dataset.
To further validate our approach, we release the dataset and invite the community to explore potential improvements.

Farmers utilize pesticides to minimize crop losses caused by pests, but these chemicals can have adverse effects on human health and the environment. Researchers are exploring more sustainable methods of pest management, such as integrating biological controls with chemical treatments. However, assessing the effectiveness of these approaches is complicated due to the variability in pest behavior and environmental conditions. This study develops a statistical model accounting for this variability, allowing for comparison of treatment performances through confidence intervals. Applying this method to strawberry disease management, findings indicate that integrated pest management reduces pesticide use without compromising fruit quality or yield.

360-degree streaming videos offer engaging and immersive virtual tourism experiences, but can be bandwidth-intensive. To optimize streaming efficiency, streaming servers pre-render entire 360-degree videos. However, this approach is impractical due to its inflexibility. Real-time streaming technology that dynamically adapts to user demand is required. A crucial optimization technique in this scenario is viewport prediction, which focuses the encoder on the area of the 360-degree video that the user is most likely to view. To achieve this, we investigated the user behavior patterns in360-degree virtual tourism videos and discovered that user viewing habits follow a subtitle-based structure, marked by distinct, fixed segments. Leveraging this insight, we developed a novel news-based encoding method that focuses on past segments, prioritizing user behavior within each segment to balance prediction accuracy and computational efficiency. This encoding method significantly reduces forecasting errors by at least 65% compared to existing techniques, substantially enhancing streaming experience without additional computational costs.

Tensor network methods have commonly been utilized in modeling different types of equilibrium and non-equilibrium situations. However, these techniques faced a critical challenge as their algorithms generally necessitated a small bond dimension at sufficiently low temperatures or time points, despite a fundamental requirement for approximating thermal states and time-evolved systems where the bond dimension is directly related to system size. This issue was tackled by constructing a specific class of objects that are able to accurately represent the thermal expectation values and time-evolved behavior for local observables in any scenario, where the bond dimension is completely independent of the system's size and is only determined by the temperature or elapsed time. Furthermore, we demonstrate the applicability of these constructed objects in approximating the thermal expectations and time evolution for a variety of models, as well as proving their internal consistency, which indicates their potential utility in calculating thermal entropy and time-generated entropy.

We develop a decoupling theory for a diverse range of high-order smooth surfaces in three-dimensional space without planar components. Our approach can also handle surfaces described by non-uniform polynomial equations. By examining these surfaces, we create an opportunity to adapt and expand the concept of linear decoupling, incorporating a combination of Taylor series analysis and the development of a library of reference surfaces to facilitate polynomial surfaces' decoupling through scaling. Ultimately, our work provides a foundation for high-order smooth surfaces' decoupling studies in three-dimensional space.

In this research, we establish a precise inequality relating anisotropic mean curvature and capacity in the L^p norm, applicable to any bounded area in R^n with smooth borders.
As a result, we derive inequalities including an anisotropic Willmore inequality, a sharp anisotropic Minkowski inequality, and a sharp volumetric anisotropic Minkowski inequality. Our proof involves a novel approach in nonlinear potential theory recently described in the reference provided.

The Microscope space test for the weak equivalence principle involves measuring tiny differences in the acceleration of two test masses as they orbit the Earth. Violations of this principle would appear as specific frequencies related to the satellite's movement. The Microscope satellite was built to minimize external forces at these key frequencies, yet unexpected sudden forces, or glitches, can still happen. These glitches need to be accounted for in the analysis to accurately interpret the test's results. Researchers are actively studying the data to better understand the causes and effects of these glitches. A significant finding from this study is that a major glitch detected in 2014 actually improved the current limits on the acceleration difference between the two test masses by a factor of three. Moving forward, analyzing glitches will be essential for accurately interpreting the results of the mission and even more so for the anticipated launch of the Microscope satellite in 2021.

We examine a rigid structure composed of two active Brownian particles that interact in an activity gradient. We demonstrate analytically that the position of the dimer varies based on the angle between the particles and accumulates either at areas with high activity levels or low activity levels. This varies according to the activity gradient strength and the angle of the dimer. Some angles result in the dimer accumulating at high activity areas, while others lead to accumulation at low activity areas, and additional angles prevent any accumulation. These outcomes are visually represented in our research through heat maps. Additionally, simulations confirm our theoretical findings.

The minimum strong shortest path cover with k-hops in a graph G is the smallest number of sets needed among all k-hops strong shortest path covers, where we also examine 2-hops covers for certain graphs and show the general k-hops cover problem is NP-complete.

The impact of infrared renormalons in the color dipole gluon distribution's variance is being quantified, and calculations demonstrate how non-linear small-x saturation impacts shift the Borel plane's initial IR pole from $2/\beta_2$ to $1/\beta_2$, thereby changing the estimated uncertainty to approximately $\Lambda_{\rm QCD}^2$ instead of $\Lambda_{\rm QCD}^4$.

As the number of frogs per site grows, the frog model's behavior shifts from transient to recurrent on a d-ary rooted tree. We determine the critical density for this transition precisely and find that it equates to the tree's degree. This study extends previous research initially proved for binary trees and now holds true for all arities.

Researchers are focusing on high-dimensional systems to better understand complex phenomena and they are offering a fresh approach by using pairs of higher-dimensional lattices as a model. In this study, the authors create and experimentally validate a specific model, a directional higher-dimensional magnetophotonic crystal, using mobile atoms in separate optical traps arranged in quadratic superpositions of 2D and reverse 2D lattices. By adjusting the relative orientation of these lattice structures, a magnetic field, and the intensity of the coupling, the researchers can manipulate the properties of a mobile particle and move it between topological phases with distinct behaviors. As a result, directional control over the mobility of the particle's state of motion is achieved based on the environment and the motion of the particle.

Knowledge distillation is a successful method for accelerating deep neural networks by training a compact model to mimic the behavior of a high-capacity network. Traditionally, this relies on having access to the original network's training data and parameters, which isn't always feasible due to storage or privacy constraints in real-world applications. This study introduces decision-based black-box knowledge distillation, allowing a model to be trained on the behavior of a network whose internal workings are inaccessible, as long as it produces classification outputs. When access to the original data is possible, a training sample's residue is calculated by comparing the target distribution with the actual distribution based on the network's output and gradient information. When only black-box access is available, the concept of virtual residue is introduced to achieve similar results. The proposed method is more efficient than alternative decision-based learning methods and surpasses traditional black-box knowledge distillation in performance.

Researchers have observed the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_S$ decay mode for the first time, and have also gathered evidence for the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_S$ decay mode, utilizing a 3.0 $\text{fb}^{-1}$ dataset of $pp$ collisions collected at 7 and 8 TeV center-of-mass energies by the LHCb. The branching fractions for these decays are calculated as follows: The $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 \bar{K}^0$ branching fraction is estimated at (4.3±0.6±0.3±0.3)×10^-4, and the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} \bar{K}^0$ branching fraction is estimated at (2.9±1.1±0.4±0.4)×10^-4, with the given uncertainties being statistical, derived from the provided data, and systematic, respectively.

Constructing the lattice of submodules of a given module is generally a challenging task. Despite the proposed method by Stanley to construct distributive lattices from their join irreducible elements, determining all join irreducible submodules of a given module is not a straightforward task. However, for modules that have specific properties, such as those arising from a particular group and characterized by multiplicity freeness, more information is available. Specifically, for such modules, all maximal and minimal submodules are made accessible, raising the question of whether this accessible information is sufficient to reconstruct the lattice of submodules. In this investigation, we focus on modules over a particular type of group and attempt to reconstruct the lattice of submodules from this accessible information for modules that are characterized by multiplicity freeness. The reconstruction is successfully achieved in the case of a particular module, but in other cases the resulting structure is only a subset of the original lattice. The difference between these cases is characterized, and the partial reconstruction of submodules for more complex modules is discussed.

A strong geodetic subset of a graph identifies all other graph vertices by specifying a set of shortest paths between selected vertices. Recent research has focused on determining which graphs can be recognized as bipartite, planar, or perfect based on their strong geodetic subsets. This paper explores the computational complexity of determining such recognition sets for a particular class of graphs. It shows that determining strong geodetic recognition is coNP-complete for graphs that are both planar and perfect, and NP-hard for graphs that are at least triangle-free. It also shows that determining strong geodetic recognition in triangle-free graphs lies within the apex of the polynomial recognition class.

The ultimate goal of imitation learning is to develop efficient policies using nearly optimal expert examples. Nonetheless, getting numerous high-quality examples from human experts is very costly, making imitation learning hard to apply in complex settings. One solution is to allow for suboptimal expert examples, including real-world human behavior that isn't always rational. Unfortunately, standard imitation learning techniques fail when faced with this kind of problem, especially in scenarios where the expert's examples don't cover all possible situations. This research proposes a novel framework, Trail, to solve this issue in a simple yet comprehensive model-checking application. We present theoretical limits for the framework's performance and propose two innovative approaches that ensure reliable performance with fewer examples, independent of the quality of the best example available.

Reinforcement learning efficiency can be significantly enhanced through imitation learning by leveraging expert guidance. However, relying on expert demonstrations is often impractical due to the high expense and unrealistic nature of the required actions in complex tasks. In this research, we introduce a pioneering co-imitation learning framework in reinforcement learning settings where agents learn to imitate unobservable expert actions by learning from actions of accessible peer actions in the absence of accessible expert demonstration. In this framework, we introduce two distinct Co-Imitation learning strategies: one employing a generative adversarial network and another based on attention mechanism. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of our methods over conventional RL and imitation learning techniques, with findings attributed to a unique error propagation phenomenon in reinforcement learning settings.

This paper proposes a metric function that yields an optimal performance on average, which significantly reduces decoding computations while maintaining excellent performance. By applying this metric, decoding computations are reduced to a fraction of the original active bits in code words, particularly in over-coded scenarios. Experimental results indicate that using this metric enhances the average decoding computations by a factor of three to four, with minimal impact on code performance. Furthermore, we provide proof that active-bit decoding is suboptimal in terms of minimum average computation, and our proposed solution does not follow this optimality.

Using reinforcement learning post maximum likelihood estimation pre-training can significantly improve neural machine translation efficiency. Nonetheless, a couple of issues hinder the practical use of RL for NMT, including the vast action space and the reliability of the reward function. This paper proposes two novel space-efficient reinforcement learning approaches, ReluAction and GroupAction, to address the large action space problem, and a self-calibration reward framework to tackle the reward reliability issue. Our experiments on the IWSLT14 French-to-en and En-to-De datasets demonstrate that our methods yield substantial improvements in translation accuracy, outperforming the baseline by up to 3.2 BLEU points, and the self-calibration reward framework leads to an 1.8 BLEU point improvement compared to the initial framework. Source code is available online.

A novel, markerless extrinsic calibration system is introduced that relies on real-world depth camera data instead of artificial markers or VR tracking devices. Machine learning models are used to develop and evaluate various systems for precise end-effector pose prediction by a robot, as well as for real-world end-effector pose estimation and the real calibration system. A unique, inhomogeneous data transformation model is developed and evaluated, allowing for the implicit estimation of real-world parameters. Experiments demonstrate the system's effectiveness, particularly in real-world scenarios. A key finding is that inhomogeneous data transformation models excel at implicit parameter estimation.

This study introduces two key concepts, quasi-finitely separating maps and quasiapproximate identities, which form the basis for the definitions of QFS-spaces and quasicontinuous maps. Building upon these definitions, various properties and characteristics of QFS-spaces are investigated. Key findings include: Firstly, any QFS-space is inherently a quasicontinuous space; secondly, closed subspaces, as well as quasicontinuous projection spaces, derived from QFS-spaces are themselves QFS-spaces; thirdly, continuous retracts of QFS-spaces possess the same characteristic and specific types of QFS-space retracts can be constructed; lastly, upper power spaces of continuous QFS-spaces correspond to FS-spaces.

The rise of partisanship seems to be rising across various metrics including voter behavior and online engagement. Research into the Web's influence on polarization has produced several key findings in the past. To build on existing research and gain deeper insights, we've studied browsing habits of thousands of users along with their online interactions with news sources. Our results reveal that users' online exposure to news sources follows distinct ideological patterns where they consistently spend more time browsing news aligned with their own viewpoint. Moreover, we've identified clear partisan groups within the broader online population based on shared browsing habits. Ultimately, we examined the impact of user decision-making on online polarization, and we've uncovered substantial evidence indicating users' deliberate actions can contribute significantly to the amplification of partisan divisions.

We examine the Lehnert and Schweitzer proof that the word problem for Thompson's group V has a non-context-free property. We further prove this word problem to be equivalent to the complement of a combined cyclic variant of several context-free languages, and for some of its generators, the combined cyclic variant of four deterministic context-free languages is sufficient. This relationship reveals that the time complexity of solving V's word problem deterministically is no more than quadratically scaling with input size.

The study of open quantum systems under periodic driving forces is highly captivating 
because, in most cases, they achieve a non-equilibrium steady state, which is
marked by a constant current. In this study, we examine discrete time-driven
dynamics in the laboratory using a single photon system that is linked to its surroundings.
Our theory is supported by experimental data and reveals that there are two distinct
periods of time in which different types of driving forces are effective.
In the first period, the system is equivalent to an open loop, 
and it responds to periodic driving forces by producing a non-zero average current. 
In the first period, the system is equivalent to an open loop, 
and it responds to periodic driving forces by producing a non-zero average current. 
By contrast, in the second period, 
the system is equivalent to a closed loop, 
and it becomes insensitive to the driving forces, 
and the average current is zero.

We explore how several established recurrent operators including curvature, Ricci, Jacobi, shape, and Weyl operators contribute substantially to biharmonic hypersurfaces being minimal within the Euclidean space.

A rational number p/q represents the basis for a numbering system. Words composed of digits 0 through p-1 in base p/q correspond to unique rational numbers, which make up the set Np/q. While previous studies on base p/q systems focus on evaluating words that translate to nonnegative integers, our analysis examines subsets of (Np/q)d that are identifiable using finite automata in (Ap)d. Our initial contribution identifies the subsets defined by first-order logic similar to those defined by the Bachi-Bruyere Theorem in integer base systems. Furthermore, our findings demonstrate that both natural order relation and modulo-q operator are not recognisable within base p/q systems.

Adding three right-handed neutrinos and a simple QCD-symmetric axial component to the Standard Model allows us to naturally set the cosmic axial dark matter density to its observed value. By limiting the axial particle's interaction with normal matter through precise tuning of one mass parameter, we can also control its density. In contrast, failing to set this parameter correctly would result in an excessively high dark matter abundance. However, if we instead focus on the neutrino sector and set two of its parameters to specific values, we can generate additional dark matter in the form of sterile neutrinos created by axial particles in early cosmic times. Interestingly, adjusting these parameters can alter the ratio of sterile neutrinos to axial particles, with far-reaching implications for both components of this two-field dark matter system.

Between October 2019 and April 2020, the LAMOST performed a unique observational study using four $K$2 plates. This study, which involved low- and medium-resolution spectroscopic surveys, gathered a significant amount of data. The low-resolution spectroscopic survey yielded around 737,000 spectra after 201 nights of 6-hour exposures. The medium-resolution spectroscopic survey took place on 100 nights with 45-minute exposures and 315 spectra were recovered. These spectra were of high quality and were used for multiple scientific studies. The data were also compared to expectations and were found to be consistent. The results were further supported by calibration tests and cross-calibration with other surveys. The research team discovered several typical scientific applications of the data, including accurate measurements of stellar properties and the prevalence of certain chemical elements in specific types of stars. The data were also used to identify variables in different types of stars and the evolution of red giant stars. The research team believed that the LAMOST time-domain survey had great potential for studying the evolution of galaxies and the properties of stellar systems.

In image recognition, distinct forms of visual cues, namely edges and textures, contribute uniquely to the overall understanding. While edges convey crucial information about a shape's form, textures reveal details about regional appearance. Current Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) applications often excel at extracting texture information but tend to produce vague boundary definitions. Expert medical analysts, for instance, primarily utilize organ edges when performing manual segmentations. Influenced by this, we developed Edge-Gated CNNs, a novel architecture that balances the extraction of both edge and texture information by initially using an edge-sensitive component to supplement a texture-focused main CNN. Our method, for instance, employs a refined edge detection technique based on edge-enhancing filters, such as Sobel and Canny, to achieve more precise and balanced feature extraction. Our proposed model demonstrated superior performance over conventional multi-channel and two-stage approaches in several medical semantic segmentation tasks, for instance, hippocampal and coronary artery tree segmentations, and outperformed existing CNNs in heart segmentation on the Cardiac Atlas Project dataset. Our model's efficiency and robustness were demonstrated through successful applications, for instance, in data-set expansions and scenarios involving a limited number of class types.

MongoDB is a widely used, document-oriented, distributed NoSQL database that allows for three different types of transactions: standalone, replica set, and sharded cluster deployments. Considering the consistency guarantees provided by MongoDB transactions in each deployment, we investigated their transactional protocols. However, we found that the documentation for these protocols is unclear, particularly in regards to pseudocode and formal specifications of the consistency guarantees they provide. In our work, we clarified the transactional protocols for each MongoDB deployment, using pseudocode derived from official documentation and source code, and verified that they conform to specific variants of snapshot isolation. Our approach also enables efficient checking of the consistency guarantees provided by MongoDB's transaction protocols.

Using the elementary symmetric function basis, we re-express the chromatic symmetric functions of Dyck paths with a bounce number of three via a combinatorial interpretation related to the inverse of the Kostka matrix from Egecioglu-Remmel (1990). This analysis shows the positivity of specific coefficients and confirms $e$-positivity for an expanded class of these functions, beyond a particular instance explored in Cho-Huh (2019).

We begin by defining a task for few-shot continual learning and propose a theory to explain how executive function works through a self-updating decision-making system that reprocesses perception data through a review of past experiences in order to minimize learning time and adapt quickly to new tasks without noticeable changes in system behavior. This idea is supported by evidence showing that humans use mental models to understand their surroundings, form conscious goals, and plan actions to influence their environment. Furthermore, research suggests that executive function emerges through neural circuits that are distinct from those processing perception. To test our theory, we demonstrate that a summary-based update process influenced by the decision-making system leads to a change in behavior, allowing a policy to automatically adjust to continual learning and perceptions, even without obvious system modifications. This summary update process achieves a policy that can understand and adapt to the environment, even when it comes to the complex field of conscious awareness.

The success of medical image analysis using machine learning largely relies on high-quality datasets.  However, when these datasets contain biases, the models can learn them, compromising their ability to generalize and produce reliable results.  While research exists on developing unbiased models, the problem lies in identifying and mitigating the inherent biases present in medical image datasets.  In an effort to address this issue, we first establish a metric to quantify data intrinsic bias and propose a new framework for detecting and quantifying biases in medical image datasets.  Our proposed framework, comprising of two sub-proposals named q-discriminator and entropy map, is designed to identify and visualize the inherent biases present in medical image datasets.  Our framework was tested on three medical image datasets, and it was able to successfully identify and visualize the biases present in them.  Moreover, we found that improving data quality by removing biased samples can lead to an improvement in model performance.  Moreover, to further advance our framework, we plan to explore other inference models and incorporate expert knowledge to validate our results.

Research on intricate systems from the human brain to social connections and biological networks has significant applications in understanding their underlying mechanisms and predicting their dynamics. To study the relationship between structure and function, researchers turned to self-organized triangular assemblies of magnetic elements triangle-based in shape. By meticulously designing an experiment to analyze a disordered system, they created a model that could explore complex dynamics through its inherent geometric properties. A critical shift in how these elements interacted due to changing assembly distances revealed a distinct transition from simple to complex behavior. Notably, this study found that certain structural features, such as isolated components and interconnected triangles, were associated with more complex activity, while other properties, including a measure of structural efficiency, demonstrated extreme values at the transition point. This empirical evidence supports the theory that the underlying geometry of complex networks significantly influences their dynamic behavior.

We studied the solar wind energy flux near the inner edge of our solar system using data from four different close approaches to the sun that occurred between 2018 and 2019. These data were collected during specific time periods and will be used to train and test the predictions of a sophisticated solar wind machine learning model. The predictions made by this model in subsequent tests matched the actual observations with high accuracy. However, the model's predictions were consistently on average lower than the actual energy flux values measured by the probes. This discrepancy is likely caused by non-Gaussian characteristics of the solar wind velocity and magnetic field strength distributions. The model predictions' standard deviations matched the actual data well, which can be applied to create confidence intervals in future uses of this model. The data used for the solar wind energy flux study are publicly accessible on the NASA Data Portal.

Thanks to speech-emotion recognition technology, computers can engage with people on a more emotional level. Nonetheless, the accuracy of speech-emotion recognition in real-world situations remains an area of improvement. One significant hurdle is the discrepancy between data collected in controlled settings and interactions with real people, which can cause our models to fail. One possible solution involves adapting the models to new environments. Nonetheless, adapting models to these new environments in real-time requires first adapting the policy and then fine-tuning the model's weights, which can be time-consuming and resource-intensive. In our approach, we develop a speech-emotion recognition framework that combines a pre-trained encoder with a novel multi-task adaptation module, allowing for efficient adaptation to different data sources. The remarkable outcome is that our proposed transformer-based encoder along with the adaptive module achieve remarkable results, outperforming existing baselines by a considerable margin. In particular, the model achieves an emotion classification accuracy of 84.58% on the Aishar1k dataset.

This paper characterizes the structural and magnetic properties of Bi-based Aurivillius material Bi$_5$FeTi$_3$O$_{15}$ under high pressure conditions. Measurements indicate that Bi$_5$FeTi$_3$O$_{15}$ exhibits a mixed valence of +2/+3 for Fe ions in its unpressurized state. Applying high pressure causes an antiferromagnetic transition in Bi$_5$FeTi$_3$O$_{15}$ to disappear and results in the development of long-range ferromagnetic order. Structural analysis also reveals two distinct phases, P2$_1$a and P2$_1$, with the latter emerging when significant P is applied (>9 GPa). The transition between these phases is marked by an abrupt increase in the P2$_1$ phase's c-axis lattice parameter. The new P2$_1$a phase exhibits ferromagnetic alignment of Fe ions. In contrast, P2$_1$a displays antiferromagnetic interactions. Bi$_5$FeTi$_3$O$_{15}$ demonstrates coexisting magnetic phases even under moderate high-pressure conditions.

Hybrid methods tackle complex shortest path problems by breaking them down into simpler, 2D subproblems. This paper analyzes the accuracy of such approximations under various edge cost function scenarios. We establish bounds on the deviation between the true and approximate path costs, as well as the spatial difference between the corresponding paths, under both bounded and linear cost functions. The developed analysis is then applied to estimate the accuracy of discretized free-flight trajectory optimization, specifically in the context of minimizing cumulative time. Numerical results are provided to illustrate the obtained bounds.

Researchers studying strong shock waves in an expanding universe have found similar results using both approximate analytical methods and full numerical simulations. The analytical solutions were obtained by applying self-similarity transformations to the governing equations, while the numerical results consistently matched the rate of change seen in the strong shock boundary. The specific self-similar solutions found are actually more widespread within the broader context of the equations being studied, and the methods used can also be applied to other scenarios involving the sudden expansion of material from a point. The results presented are also being compared to those from a previously studied scenario with different boundary conditions. The findings will contribute to a deeper understanding of the Craik instability phenomenon.

Using 13 TeV proton-proton collision data, specifically 1.7 inverse femtobarns of luminosity collected by the LHCb detector, the shape of the $B_s^0\rightarrow D_s^{*-}\mu^+\nu_{\mu}$ differential decay rate is determined as a function of hadron recoil. This rate is fitted to verify the capacity of the DFL model at next-to-leading order in the strong interaction theory to predict the rate's behavior. The analysis involves identifying $D_s^{-}$ mesons via their decay into $K^{-}\kappa^{+}$ final states, along with $D_s^{*-}$ decaying into $D_s^{-}\gamma$ or $D_s^{-}$ plus soft photons, enabling the extraction of the rate from fully reconstructed $B_s^0$ decays. This in turn enables determination of the form factors within the DFL model.

A recent paper provides an analysis of advancements made in categorizing monodromy-free Schrödinger operators with rational potential properties. A specific subset of potential properties is studied which comprise generalized Hermite polynomials, constructed through the use of Wronskians from classical Hermite polynomials. These polynomials were previously shown to be related to monodromy-free Schrödinger operators with rational potential properties, however, their generation was limited to specific orders using the Askey-Wilson $q$-difference operator's factorization properties. This research expands upon their general formula, allowing for an examination of generalized Hermite polynomials derived from any interlacing family of Askey-Wilson polynomials. Such an exploration leads to the discovery of new, monodromy-free Schrödinger operators with rational potential properties, furthering our understanding of this subfield.

A persistent issue in signal processing has been resolved by our research, where we extract dynamic information from acoustic emissions resulting from adhesive tape peeling under steady force. Through phase space reconstruction, our findings reveal the deterministic chaotic nature of these dynamics by confirming the existence of a correlation dimension and a positive Lyapunov exponent at specific traction velocities. The outcomes are supported by a theoretical model highlighting the deterministic source of acoustic emissions and potential applications in material science and biology.

In epitaxial InAs/Al structures, our experimental analysis reveals the stochastic behavior of planar Josephson junctions and SQUIDs as temperature varies, exhibiting a crossover between macroscopic quantum tunneling and phase diffusion. The threshold temperature for this phase transition can be manipulated by adjusting a gate. The observed diffusion exponent of 1.5 aligns with nonperturbative theory predictions and marks the beginning of a regime where more intricate quantum phase transitions may lie.

The Yang-Mills-aether theory is analyzed to understand the implications of introducing non-abelian aether-like terms that violate Lorentz symmetry, specifically within thermal quantum field theory. By incorporating temperature effects and spatial compactification via Thermofield Dynamics, corrections to the non-abelian Stefan-Boltzmann law and non-abelian Casimir energy and pressure are calculated for both zero and finite temperatures.

This research develops a method for estimating the expected cost of hedging European options through the delta-hedging process, resulting in a computationally efficient formula that accounts for option prices and the behavior of delta processes. Initially, a standard unit hedging cost is established and subsequently, the total hedging cost is determined as the product of this unit cost, stock price, and an integer representing net shares transacted per unit time. The anticipated values of finite sums involving stock prices and gamma distributed random variables are calculated explicitly. The proposed formula is then utilized to compute hedging costs for commonly traded options and the results are compared to existing methods and Monte Carlo simulations. The resulting data are presented in easily accessible tables to facilitate quick retrieval by market practitioners.

By applying variational techniques, we develop a limiting model for a set of functionals subject to linear differential constraints. This framework models the energy of a heterogeneous material with a high-contrast composite structure at a microscopic scale, comprising a periodically perforated matrix filled with a dissimilar substance. Our key finding involves analyzing the $\Gamma$-convergence as the material periodicity diminishes, demonstrating that the limit functional comprises two components: the stored energy within the matrix, and the stored energy within the fillings. To overcome the coercivity issue inherent in the material structure, we employ two-scale convergence methods, while novel results are established for addressing the linear differential constraints via existence proofs for potentials and constraint-preserving extension operators.

We undertook a statistical investigation into tidal features surrounding early-type galaxies of massive proportions, utilizing data from the Hyper Suprime-Cam Subaru Strategic Program. Our analysis revealed that roughly 25 percent of these galaxies, with masses exceeding 10^11 solar masses, exhibit tidal features accounting for more than 10 percent of their total flux. Our findings indicate tidal features are more frequent in galaxies with low specific stellar formation rates and extreme masses. Our data also suggest that the tidal features surrounding these galaxies are typically insignificant, extending no more than 20 percent of their effective radius. Our analysis also revealed the tidal features surrounding these galaxies are highly visible even from considerable distances. Subsequently, we employed tidal features to estimate the merger rates of these galaxies and found that the average merger rates for massive galaxies have declined since a look-back time of 6 billion years. Our findings indicate the merger rates for these galaxies with masses exceeding 10^11 solar masses are approximately 6.5 percent per gigayear. Our findings suggest their merger rates are comparable to those of more intermediate mass galaxies but significantly exceed the merger rates of lower mass galaxies.

A higher education system or similar opportunities can drive social mobility across generations by allowing individuals to rise above their family's economic status. To examine this dynamic in societies with social mobility limitations, a new model allocates opportunities to maximize the benefits they provide to current and future generations. Our model reveals that, in order to maximize long-term payoffs, it's beneficial to give priority to lower socioeconomically situated individuals who have greater potential to rise to better socioeconomical standings. The result can lead to scenarios where those from wealthier backgrounds are more likely to benefit from opportunities, as they often have a higher chance of succeeding and passing on the benefits to their offspring. Various factors, including the degree of intermarriage and the length of generational cycles, can influence the various equilibrium outcomes possible.

The combination of chirped pulse amplification and nonlinear optical systems has been the foundation for significant progress in numerous sectors, including semiconductors, communications, biology, defense, and national security. However, accurately modeling these laser systems using CPA and NLO is a complex task due to their interconnected linear and nonlinear processes, and the high variability in available modeling techniques. The authors present a unified mathematical model for modeling and optimizing high-power laser systems based on CPA and NLO, and explore its applications, including the reverse engineering of Ti:Sa laser systems producing 100-fs pulses with 120 kW average power. Through the implementation of a novel modeling framework, the researchers successfully replicated key parameters of this laser system, including its 800-nm pulse spectrum and 120-kW average power output.

We maintain fixed $p$ values and let $\varepsilon$ values vary. It is demonstrated that for any incompressible subset $X$ of $\ell_p$, there exists a map $f$ targeting $\ell_{q(p,\varepsilon)}$ with a specific distortion characteristic. The target space $\ell_{q(p,\varepsilon)}$ contains a compressed image of $X$ with a dimension reduction of a constant factor. The relationship between $q(p,\varepsilon)$ and its variables has a graphical representation. The map's distortion is subsequently analyzed for an alternative definition of incompressibility based on volume preservation, with a comparison made to a relevant theorem from Ref. -like source material.

In 2015, CERN introduced "Emittance Scans," a new fast luminosity separation scanning method at the Large Hadron Collider. These scans were consistently carried out during physics production runs, utilizing full-intensity beams at the CMS experiment's interaction point. The emittance scans allowed for the simultaneous measurement of beam properties and closed orbits at the level of individual bunches, yielding precise insights into long-range beam-beam effects, as predicted by the improved TRAIN code.

This paper explores the optimization challenges in multi-agent systems that involve agents behaving maliciously, which leads to a misdirection of the group towards an undesired solution or system paralysis through actions like blocking communication and injecting false data. To address this issue, we develop a distributed optimization algorithm based on gradient updates suitable for scenarios where some agents have prior knowledge of the optimal solution and can freely share this information with others, thereby facilitating faster convergence. Our proposed method guarantees that the system will reach the optimal solution even in the presence of malicious agents, assuming they are limited in number, and allows for regulation of the impact of their actions by adjusting the algorithm's parameters. Furthermore, we present a performance analysis of the algorithm that will be感兴趣 to researchers, and potentially demonstrate it through simulations.

The study of cosmic microwave background anisotropies is a fundamental tool in physical cosmology research. However, the signal's weakness necessitates sophisticated and highly sensitive experiments that observe the sky across various frequencies with thousands of polarisation-sensitive detectors. As such experiments become increasingly sensitive, they are susceptible to being limited by instrumental systematic effects when trying to fully utilise their data. This paper presents a Python tool, s4cmb, for realistically simulating instrument systematic effects in future cosmic microwave background experiments. The simulation includes cross-talk between modes, random errors, and detector noise in s4cmb. The documentation and sample simulation code for instrument systematic effects in the S4, CMB-S4, and other experiments are included with this tool.

In the task of arranging unordered words into a meaningful order, prior approaches rely on either linear models or neural networks, without examining the role of pre-trained language models, including why they would be beneficial. Utilizing BART as an example, we find it to be a suitable model for this task and explore its capabilities by conducting additional analysis using probing, which reveals that the syntactic dependencies inherent to BART significantly contribute to its performance. Furthermore, we discover improvements in using BART in a related task known as partial tree linearization.

The rapid dissemination of ultra-realistic media over social platforms necessitates the immediate development of an efficient and adaptable technique for identifying deepfakes. Deepfake creation methods generate realistic forgeries by synthesizing images or audio from multiple sources, but these methods often leave subtle anomalies that native recording devices do not produce. Recently, research has focused on physical and physiological inconsistencies in deepfake images, yet these approaches struggle with multilayered neural networks and have limited applicability to video content. This paper presents a novel detection technique called the MD-CSDNetwork, a cross-stitched network that operates across the entire magnitude domain in an end-to-end manner. The proposed model employs two synchronized sub-networks to capture low and high-frequency details in deepfake images, respectively, and incorporates attention mechanisms to pinpoint regions with physiological discrepancies. Experimental results using public deepfake datasets demonstrate that the MD-CSDNetwork outperforms leading classifiers in accuracy and exhibits enhanced performance in video detections.

Current studies examining the performance of randomly assembled low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes usually assume the independence of degree distributions from edge endpoints. In contrast, our research extends these assumptions by modeling the independence between degree distributions and edge endpoints using a tripartite graph, specifically binary tripartite graphs. Our analysis of binary erasure channels leads to novel ensembles of LDPC codes and their corresponding decoding thresholds. Notably, these new ensembles, including those with uncorrelated degree distributions, edges, or merely independent degree correlations, are shown to be suboptimal. The findings suggest that LDPC code enamples featuring low-degree correlations may exist that surpass the capabilities of traditional randomly assembled LDPC code enamples characterized by independently separated degree distributions.

A critical flaw exists in the current application of quantum key distribution (QKD) systems due to their vulnerability to quantum hacking. Our novel approach incorporates a hybrid measurement attack, achievable with only standard components, accounting for the use of photon number splitting attacks and coherent-state attacks. We develop an updated bound on secret key rate that accounts for this attack, leveraging information gained from intensity measurement data. Zhan's proposed defense, involving randomization of the quantum signal's phase for single photons, is adapted and enhanced in our work. Our novel scheme demonstrates the ability to regain the performance of the decoy-state protocol with full phase randomization, without compromising the system's overall performance.

To effectively manage the vast amounts of data being generated by a growing number of mobile devices, traditional core networks must undergo significant upgrades in both capacity and efficiency. In addition, the high energy consumption of these core networks poses a major operational expense and environmental concern. This research proposes a novel, energy-efficient and adaptive core network management approach, which is designed to address these issues. The proposed solution is based on a software-defined network architecture and utilizes machine learning algorithms to optimize energy consumption and adapt to changing network conditions. A key feature of this approach is its ability to dynamically control the use of energy-consuming components, such as network links and processors, to reduce overall energy consumption. Furthermore, the proposed solution is able to adapt to changing traffic patterns and network conditions, allowing it to maintain high levels of efficiency over time. Ultimately, this research demonstrates the potential for machine learning-based core network management approaches to deliver on their promise of delivering energy-efficient and sustainable mobile data networks.

In 1930, mathematician K. Menger developed an interest in the abstract concept of angle function, which he then generalized for use in metric and semi-metric spaces. Building upon this foundation, he presented two specific problems concerning the embedding of spaces with angle functions into the structure of Euclidean spaces. Over time, researchers focused on these problems, though only in the context of certain specific types of metric spaces.
