A blockchain-based smart contract is an automated transaction program, utilized in various cryptocurrencies, that is a high-stakes form of untrusted code. A mistaken program can result in financial losses. A verifier is an analytical tool used to ensure the correctness of a transaction program according to a specified purpose, and we have developed a novel checker for the Tezos programming language, a functional language used for creating transaction contracts on the Tezos blockchain. Our tool utilizes a set of sophisticated types, including custom-made "refinement types" that encode additional information about a transaction contract, and it leverages a technique known as "program rewriting" to transform a transaction contract into a refined program with a guaranteed level of safety. Our checker is among a select few capable of confirming the correctness of an actual transaction contract and capable of automatically identifying and rectifying errors in the code. Our tool has been successfully applied to multiple transaction contracts including the famous Catastrophe Insurance contract, a collective investment scheme, and various other contracts used for waste management, rehabilitation, and asset management, and it has been made publicly available for download from the GitHub repository https://github.com/TezosFEP/helmholtz.

Deep Neural Network structures, specifically Graph Convolutional Neural Networks (GCNNs), have gained popularity in processing complex and irregular data patterns, despite the limited understanding of their fundamental workings due to their opaque nature. We investigate the inner mechanics of GCNNs, showcasing how various filtering techniques affect performance, with a focus on graph convolutional operations as a means of implementing matchable filters. Experimental evidence from diverse applications, including node classification, supports this approach, and a theoretical framework based on the spectral properties of the graph provides additional support. The application of GCNNs in node classification demonstrates our point and successfully enhances existing models by incorporating custom-designed filters.

In a three-dimensional spacetime, Einstein's gravity theory is replaced by Chern-Simons gauge theory using SO(2,1) symmetry as the underlying structure. The resulting high-temperature 'hairy' black hole solutions described by scalar fields emerge from an effective non-relativistic Chern-Simons gauge theory, so long as the scalar field's mass term respects the symmetry. If the scalar field's mass term breaks the symmetry, the corresponding Chern-Simons gauge theory becomes inapplicable. However, by extending the theory to include an additional degree of freedom in its symmetry group, we can recover the original symmetry-breaking 'hairy' black hole solutions, as well as their symmetry-respecting counterparts and scalar field condensates in the absence of matter. Lastly, by incorporating an Abelian U(1) gauge field into our theory, we can describe black holes with rotating hair that involve charge densities.

Theories of supersymmetric Yang-Mills with algebra so(4N) can have non-trivial, invertible-defying symmetries. By utilizing holographic duality, we can determine the branes equivalent to these symmetries, and deduce the fusion principles for the symmetries through brane dynamics.

Elastography, an advanced imaging technique, utilizes ultrasound to visualize and measure tissue properties, utilizing strain and tissue displacement to assess mechanical properties and the material's influence on sound waves. The accuracy of recovered parameters relies heavily on precise strain and displacement estimation, particularly for stiffer tissues and areas with higher strain rates. One limiting factor in strain estimation is the inability of conventional ultrasound methods to accurately measure tissue displacement in the lateral direction due to inadequate spatial sampling. This study presents a novel technique called Virtual Source Synthetic Aperture (VSSA), which enhances lateral displacement estimation by using a data acquisition method that synthesizes ultrasound data as if it originated from non-physical virtual sources. The VSSA approach utilizes full matrix capture (FMC) data to create high-resolution beams with very low angles of incidence, resulting in sub-wavelength accuracy in 1D displacement estimation. The resolution of the VSSA method is analyzed and compared to other approaches, including the VSSA element and the wide beam approaches, the VSSA approach was also used in a synthetic elastography framework to recover tissue density, friction coefficient, and modulus in periodic media, the improvement in accuracy in all recovered parameters is attributed to the increased resolution of the VSSA approach.

Imperative algorithms and logical proofs in sequent calculus or natural deduction coexist as distinct yet related concepts. This interconnection suggests a fundamental equivalence, which we can express as the notion that imperative algorithms essentially embody a form of proofs with cut operations. This equivalence serves as the foundation for an expanded framework, which we call "logical pseudocodes." Each statement in logical pseudocodes is analogous to a step in natural deduction, ensuring correctness and safety in accordance with the original specifications. This approach can be seen as a natural extension to the concept of a computability logic web, but now incorporating the capacity for forward reasoning.

The concept of Boolean Ramsey numbers for sets of posets was initially explored in relation to Boolean lattices and posets obtained from chains with minimal elements combined into an 'N-shaped order' or 'V-shaped order'. A key objective is to establish the Boolean Ramsey property for such posets, and while recent studies have focused on determining growth rates for posets with this property, another area of interest is investigating whether Boolean Ramsey numbers for such a poset and its superposets remain bounded, and if so, whether they can be bounded by any integer greater than one. This line of research is relevant in relation to recent breakthrough findings in Boolean representation of posets and partial orders. In this study, we examine Boolean Ramsey numbers for sets of V-shaped posets and both their minimum and body components separately, deriving representations for such sets with specific Boolean isomorphic two-posets and a family of binary trees with analogous properties.

In the context of dynamic data streams, where Euclidean space points are added or removed from a dataset, we develop a one-pass coreset algorithm for solving the $k$-means clustering problem. Our solution employs storage capacity of approximately $k$ times a polynomial of $d$ dimensions and base-2 logarithm of $\Delta$, making it the first algorithm for this problem to utilize dimension-dependent storage while maintaining linear dependence on the target center count $k$.

We introduce a novel hierarchical strategy for resolving large-scale discrete stochastic pursuit-evasion games on grid worlds by subdividing the environment into'macro-states'. Each state in a smaller-subgrid corresponds to a single state in the larger grid, enabling partial observability. We develop two complementary policies: a finer-grained solver addresses the smaller game within each macro-state, while a coarser solver decides transitions between macro-states based on observed states within each corresponding micro-grid. Combining these policies using Bayesian inference creates a player-device scenario where the device executes the solver and reports observations to the player, guaranteeing optimal performance. We present this hierarchy of solvers analytically and through examples. Moreover, we explore reducing the cognitive load on the device and experiment with additional solvers, a lightweight best-fit solver, and a direct reinforcement learning approach, supportting the hierarchy with reinforcement learning tests. Our results demonstrate the hierarchy's viability and the advantages of using optimal policies over suboptimal ones and direct reinforcement learning.

The concept of cycles in social interactions lacks clarity, which is evident from the varying definitions of cyclicity found in literature. One such definition, known as weak cyclicity, has been addressed by removing a specific influence identified by Tognetti and Tasso, leading to the development of acyclic probabilities. Building upon this, we introduce the framework of nontransitive relations and their associated nontransitive probabilities. A new, distinct approach to cyclicity is presented, and its relationship to the previously discussed definition of weak cyclicity is discussed. Furthermore, we provide examples of nontransitive mechanisms, including dice, as well as a mathematical model of social interactions represented by a Gaussian chain, along with an examination of its relationship to the previously discussed definition of cyclicity.

Recently, deep learning techniques have gained popularity for enhancing low-dose CT images, particularly due to their impressive performance at a relatively low computational cost. A key method in this area, the unsupervised cycleGAN approach, has shown promise in improving the efficiency of clinical workflows. However, its performance can be hindered by a lack of sufficient training data and limited generalization capabilities across various protocols. This work presents a new implementation of cycleGAN that utilizes two forms of attention mechanisms to overcome these limitations. By combining adaptation of style information and prioritizing latent features that differentiate input images, this method eliminates the need for explicit domain cycles while maintaining cycle-consistency in enhanced images. The proposed method, AdSwitchLC, was tested on liver CT images and demonstrated superior performance to the cycleGAN baseline, with improved dice similarity and mean squared error metrics.

Recent advancements in task-oriented dialog understanding have been achieved through pre-training methods, however, they depend heavily on large annotated datasets which become expensive at the marginally annotated data rate. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a novel framework called SPACE-2 (Pre-trained Semi-supervised Contrastive) that combines several cutting-edge techniques including tree-structured semi-supervised pre-training, contrastive learning, and dropout-based data augmentation. This framework is designed to enhance representation learning even with limited annotated training sets. We integrate these methods to build a cohesive pre-training system and demonstrate its efficacy in task-oriented dialog understanding through the multi-task MUCALo dialog understanding benchmark. Our results show significant improvements in accuracy, with notable gains even with only single-task annotated data. We open-source our model to facilitate future research in this area at https://github.com/ChenShi2017/SPACE-2.

This research aims to examine the geometric makeup of an ideal fluid's spacetime 
when coupled with a torsion-forming vector field and the conformal Ricci-Yamabe 
soliton. We use a conformal metric transformation to derive the Yamabe soliton 
equation and analyze its resulting Yamabe constant. Additionally, this study 
seeks to clarify the relationship between the Yamabe soliton and various other 
geometric properties, including the shrinking, expanding, and steady states of the 
soliton, as well as its soliton geodesic equation and curvature function.

To study the rotational characteristics of distorted halos, we utilized the angular momentum projection method on wave functions derived from the deformed relativistic Hartree-Bogoliubov theory in continuum. Our self-consistent approach effectively accounts for interactions between single particle bound states and the continuum across ground and rotational states. By analyzing rotational states in isotopes of $^{42}$Mg and $^{44}$Mg, specifically excitation energy, configuration, and density distribution, our research demonstrates that deformed halo structures endure from intrinsic ground states to collective rotational states, particularly illustrating shape decoupling effects in rotating distorted halo nuclei.

A common approach in video super-resolution is the recurrent structure, with the BasicVSR method being one of the top-performing frameworks, leveraging bidirectional propagation and feature alignment to exploit temporal information in video signals. In our research, we upgrade BasicVSR by incorporating second-order propagation and a refined alignment strategy known as cross-channel alignment, resulting in our enhanced model, BasicVSR++, which is available as an open-source implementation. Comparative experiments demonstrate that BasicVSR++ outperforms the original BasicVSR and other leading video super-resolution models, with objective metrics showing a significant improvement in performance of around 0.2-0.3 ratios on video super-resolution benchmarks, and better preservation of structural and textual details in video sequences according to subjective assessments.

Due to the tendency for high-energy lepton colliders to radiate forward and resemble weak boson colliders beyond a few TeV, a new perspective is taken to treat weak bosons as composite entities that form the basis of a weak boson parton distribution at lepton-lepton interactions. This paper introduces a novel, simplified method to calculate the weak boson PDF at such interactions, adapting the 'Vector Boson Approximation' and developing the effective VBA (eVBA). The effective VBA is found to closely align with the standard method of deriving weak boson PDFs, and even FD merging with the latter shows the standard approach, indicating that eVBA can serve as a practical framework for weak boson PDFs at high-energy muon colliders.

In multi-task reinforcement learning, using shared representations can greatly
benefit a learner when it comes to solving a variety of tasks. While this
synergy is evident in model-free methods using shared policy networks, our study
investigates the benefits of shared dynamics models in model-based multi-task
reinforcement learning settings. Surprisingly, our findings indicate that using
a single learned dynamics model for solving multiple tasks often causes
significant performance decline when the tasks are or when the tasks are only
slightly related. To overcome this challenge, we propose separating the learning
process into two parts: by modularizing the dynamics models, each module can be
specialized for a particular task without causing performance degradation. We
showcase the theoretical underpinnings of our approach, analyzing how optimal
modularity emerges from the need to learn several tasks at once. Furthermore, we
demonstrate its practical application in a module specialization framework for
model-based multi-task reinforcement learning, showing that optimal Zermelo
navigation can be achieved by modular policies when tasks are learned
independently. Lastly, we evaluate our approach on continuous control tasks and
find evidence that increased modularity leads to better generalization and more
effective transfer of policies between tasks.

The paper provides derivations of Li-Yau and Souplet-Zhang type estimates for the equation $u_t=\Delta_\xi p + \lambda u + A(u)$ in a complete, non-compact metric measure space with compact boundary. Furthermore, the paper includes local gradient estimates for the equation $\Delta_\xi(u^p)+\lambda u + A(u) = 0$ on complete, non-compact manifolds with compact boundary.

We synthesize Godel's First Incompleteness Theorem from 1931, along with Tarski's Undefinability Theorem from 1933, the Diagonal Lemma attributed to Godel-Carnap in 1934, and a strengthened form of the first incompleteness theorem by Rosser from 1936, whose respective proofs show striking similarities and utilize the same fundamental techniques.

This paper formulates the three balls theorem for functions u, subject to specific conditions derived from Clifford analysis. In particular, we leverage these conditions to extend Hadamard's three circles theorem to monogenic functions within R^n+1 space.

When the population is not fully known in advance, sampling occurs in sequence, either individually or in batches, which are obtained one after another. This work presents a novel algorithm that allows for sequential selection of a balanced sample. The algorithm accommodates equal-sized or unequal-sized units, and is capable of processing the population in sequence, either individually or in batches. Additionally, this work provides theoretical justification for the accuracy of the proposed algorithm, and an example is provided to illustrate its application.

In robotics, calibrating an eye-in-hand camera using image information is an essential task that has been extensively researched. We investigated using artificial intelligence-based methods for this purpose by leveraging only a single color image, utilizing exclusively simulated data to train the models. Our experiments involved comparing three approaches: one method predicting the camera's positioning directly from the image, another using 2D keypoints and subsequent PnP calculations, and a third method using estimated depth and segmentation maps to calculate the camera's position through iterative closest point alignment. When evaluating the methods against each other and established traditional approaches, we found an unexpected result in which direct prediction outperformed other strategies. Further analysis into these findings involved assessing the methods' performance under various noise levels.

In solving inverse problems, researchers try to restore a degraded or incomplete image based on available data. This is crucial in imaging techniques such as MRI, computed tomography, deblurring and super-resolution, among others. Because there can be multiple plausible images given the measurements and prior information, the focus should not just be on recovering a single solution but rather on sampling from a distribution representing all viable options, which is essential for uncertainty assessment in imaging and non-imaging applications. This study explores and evaluates techniques for efficiently sampling from the posterior distribution of unknown variables in inverse problems, particularly using a regularized conditional generative adversarial network (GAN) model. Unlike conventional standalone regularized GAN approaches, this method demonstrates a regularized conditional GAN can effectively generate diverse, high-quality samples in testing scenarios including MRI with compressed sensing, image deblurring and convolutional neural network inversion, after evaluating both Bernoulli and logistic formulations for the discriminator.

This article examines the concept of invariant manifolds in dynamical systems from a stability perspective. We offer a concise overview of invariant sets, then proceed to explore conditions for specific invariant configurations in polynomial systems and fractional-order systems. Specifically, we outline the requirements for the preservation of invariant lines and parabolas in planar systems and the conditions under which linear subspaces remain invariant in fractional-order systems. We also discuss a notable result highlighting the limitations of such invariance in certain types of fractional systems.

Next-generation wireless networks will utilize Terahertz frequencies to significantly boost data transfer speeds, yet signal degradation at THz frequencies necessitates extensive beam management. Traditional wide-range beam searching methods are inefficient due to their time-consuming nature, prompting researchers to explore machine learning techniques for improved performance. This paper proposes a novel approach using reinforcement learning to accelerate beam discovery in THz links by initially learning and utilizing optimal beam pairs from lower GHz links in a multi-hop setup. Simulation results indicate that such reinforcement learning-based beam optimization can achieve near-optimal performance with significantly reduced overhead. Furthermore, the introduction of a refined reward mechanism in the learning process accelerates convergence and yields superior results compared to conventional reinforcement learning approaches.

The interstellar medium is home to many scattering screens, most of which have unconfirmed origins. Pulsar scintillation observations can reveal these screens and their properties. This paper analyzes 23 years of data from Arecibo observations of the pulsar PSR B1133+16 at a wavelength of 0.2 meters. A total of 154,812 individual screen velocity distributions were collected, and their characteristics in drift rate, tilt, and shape were mapped across the sky in the pulsar's line of sight. A comparison was made with optical observations of the same region, as well as Arecibo and ALEXIS scans conducted at 0.3 and 0.5 meters, respectively. The Arecibo scans at 0.2 meters provided unusually clear broad screen structures, allowing detailed study of their trajectories. In contrast to a previous study using shorter observation times and lower resolution conducted at 0.3 meters, the results showed distinct broad screen morphologies and locations. In addition, a new distant screen was discovered for the first time. These findings highlight the detailed information about the interstellar medium that can be obtained from high-resolution, long-duration observations conducted with the Arecibo telescope before its collapse.

This paper presents a generative model called Quasi-Periodic WaveNet (QPNet) to enhance the limited pitch control of WaveNet (WN) through pitch-dependent dilated convolution neural networks. WN achieves high-fidelity audio generation using stacked dilated convolution layers as an autoregressive probabilistic model. However, the lack of prior knowledge and the pure data-driven nature of WN lead to pitch control difficulties, particularly in modeling periodic signal components for inputs outside the training frequency range. To overcome this challenge, QPNet is proposed with two innovations. Firstly, the network adapts to given pitch information by modifying the dilation factors of convolutions guided by a cosine function that captures the signal's quasi-periodic nature. Secondly, a tailored network structure reduces redundant computation in time-series processing by considering the known frequency information. Experimental results using MNIST and LibriSpeech datasets show the advantages of QPEN over WN in generation speed and quality.

This research presents a novel annotation and correction tool for Arabic texts,
namely MADARi, catering to Standard and Dialectal varieties. MADARi offers a user-
friendly interface and efficient management capabilities for annotating and handling
a considerable volume of texts. Its key features encompass a range of morphological
annotations, such as analyzing dialectal texts for part-of-speech, sentence structure,
and root patterns. MADARi offers a set of pre-defined options to expediate the
annotation and review processes, resulting in enhanced productivity. The system
also offers a set of essential APIs to facilitate seamless integration with existing
projects, which have already been utilized in several integration scenarios for
annotating large datasets, such as dialectal novels and news articles.

Planets situated in the habitable zone of their host stars may experience photochemistry that could impact their habitability. This process, driven by stellar radiation, primarily in the ultraviolet spectrum, can influence atmospheric composition and create photochemical products observable through spectroscopy. A model combining radiative transfer and chemical modeling is presented to analyze photochemistry in temperate, gas-rich exoplanets with either hot-Jupiter or super-Earth/Neptune characteristics. These planets were studied at equilibrium and inclined temperatures across a wide spectrum of irradiation levels and host star types. Irradiation levels were quantified using the Sola index, while mass ratios, relevant for specific planetary types, were also incorporated into the analysis. For highly irradiated planets, especially those around M-dwarf stars with Sqa indices above 10^10, extensive atomic hydrogen was detected due to H2 photodissociation, alongside enhanced C/O ratios resulting from CO breakdown, while CH4 remained intact due to lack of photolysis, despite extensive C2H2 and CO2 formation. For less irradiated planets, solar-level photochemistry showed characteristic spectral absorption of major atmospheric components, NH3, H2O, CH4, as well as more complex molecules like C2H2, C2H4, CO2, and N2O. Notably, certain complex hydrocarbons, including C4H6 and C6H6, were found under specific conditions, while their nucleation

To differentiate between zero-energy peaks originating from Majorana and those from other causes at non-zero temperatures, our method involves swapping the normal lead in tunneling spectroscopy with a high-resistance lead (characterized by large Ohm values). The increased resistance in this setup significantly alters tunneling conductance, impacting it in distinct ways. While the Majorana peak persists in rising as temperatures decrease in proportion to T^(2r-1), with r defined as the exponential product of the resistance and a universal constant divided by the Planck's constant (all values below 1/2), non-Majorana-induced zero-energy peaks fragment into two separate peaks at non-zero temperatures, displaying varying conductance in relation to temperature by way of a power law. Furthermore, tunneling associated with a Majorana mode falls within the same broad class of universal behaviors as does the case for unstable critical points with a non-Majorana mode.

The development of advanced detection algorithms through deep learning has accelerated the identification of road issues, including automatic defect detection and marking analysis. To expedite and reduce costs associated with manual inspections, a comprehensive system called RoadAtlas has been developed, providing a holistic solution encompassing road flaw detection, marking parsing, interactive data visualization through a web interface, and a robust database framework supported by API tools.

The theory of shadows constitutes an axiomatic bicategorical framework, extending and matching key characteristics of topological Hochschild homology (THH), notably preserving properties akin to Morita invariance. Through the incorporation of Berman's extension of THH to bicategories, it is demonstrated that functors from the THH of a bicategory are equivalent to shadows of that bicategory, ultimately establishing a direct relationship between them. Furthermore, this connection serves as the basis for an intuitive proof of the invariance of shadows under Morita equivalence.

Our primary goal in this research is to pinpoint sound sources within video frames without relying on manually labeled data. Our core innovation involves training the network to distinguish between difficult image elements, including those that include the object generating the sound, to significantly enhance sound source localization performance. To achieve this, we introduce a self-supervised technique called Difficulty-Aware Region Enhancement (DARE), an auxiliary task designed to capture challenging visual areas from audio-visual data without manual labeling. For a more comprehensive result, DARE areas can be combined with regions identified through traditional Sound Source Localization (SSL). Experimentally, our method's regions show a 3.6-fold improvement in F1-score over existing unsupervised approaches on the HUDL10 dataset, and also excel in solving the hard cases that the existing unsupervised methods struggle with. Moreover, our method's performance on the complex scenes of the AMI-HUDL dataset surpasses the current unsupervised baseline models.

Recent advancements in graph convolutional networks (GCNs) have been primarily based on Euclidean geometry, but such methods may suffer from significant distortions when dealing with scale-free or hierarchical graphs. Researchers have proposed GCNs in non-Euclidean geometry, specifically in hyperbolic space, and have achieved notable performance improvements. However, existing hyperbolic graph operations fail to accurately follow the principles of hyperbolic geometry, potentially hindering the efficacy of these networks. This paper presents a novel hyperbolic GCN (L-GCN) inspired by GCNs linearised by the nearness-preserving projection, and addresses the issues of distorted graph operations. L-GCN is equipped with various lorentzian graph convolutions and can be theoretically analysed through the graph neural tangent flow theory. Empirical evidence from semi-supervised node classification and transductive link prediction tasks demonstrates the superiority of L-GCN over existing methods in various hyperbolic space RNNs.

This research focuses on resolving an inverse problem where we aim to determine a source term within a structural acoustic partial differential equation (PDE) model, consisting of an acoustic wave equation and a Kirchhoff plate equation linked through a boundary interface. Uniqueness and a stability estimate for the source term can be established using a single measurement of the structure's boundary values. This uniqueness proof relies on the Carleman estimate, and subsequent stability results stem from observability inequality and a compactness-uniqueness argument. An operator theoretical approach provides the regularity needed for initial conditions, thereby obtaining the desired stability estimate.

A new method has been created that successfully transfers squeezed states into optical cavities even in stable conditions. The method builds upon conventional optomechanical setups, utilizing a three-level atom to facilitate the transfer. Two techniques were devised to observe the transfer effect, including applying a controlled magnetic field and utilizing optical sidebands. Mathematical analysis demonstrated the ability to produce the desired squeezed state transfer in the optomechanical system under a specific level of squeezing input, successfully achieved in a simulation within a reasonable timeframe. The method's ability to reproduce the theoretical results in an experimental setting was also confirmed. The developed approach has significant implications for efficient generation of squeezed states in optomechanical systems, crucial for advancing quantum computing and optical measurements. The method's success in achieving stable state transfer was further confirmed through experimental validation. The developed approach's ability to produce the desired squeezed state transfer in the optomechanical system was also confirmed through simulation. We examine an expansion of modal $\mu$-calculus, specifically considering its application to sets comprised of fundamental elements. Following a transcription of modal $\mu$-calculus over pairs, we look at basic forms and explore general formulas. General formulas can be simplified to a combination of formulas involving basic structures, which can be further simplified to a combination of atomic formulas. Atomic formulas represent the most basic form of expression containing $\text{B$\mu$}@$. Furthermore, general formulas can be derived from modal $\mu$-calculus expressions through equivalence, making it impossible for negative cyclic definitions to be simple. This impossibility is demonstrated for both vectorial and scalar formulations of modal $\mu$-calculus with atoms, even in their binary versions.

We present a novel exponential delay discounting model incorporating
variations in impulsivity, which is analogous to the 2007 Tsallis delay discounting
model proposed by Takahashi, with a dual nature. We show that our model's
parameters correlate with the average and standard deviation of impulsivity, and
these results provide a clear path for investigating the Tsallis distribution in a
social context.

When considering linearized gravity within a harmonic gauge theory for a symmetric tensor field, implementing the harmonic gauge yields multiple gauge options, resulting in the gauge appearing as a class rather than a singular choice.  This feature provides a physical justification for adopting a specific covariant harmonic gauge that arises when a mass term is added to the gravitational perturbation.  Specifically, one particular choice of harmonic gauge leads to a linearized massive gravity model with the correct five degrees of freedom and avoids the vDVZ discontinuity, in contrast to the standard Fierz-Pauli theory.

A signed graph is created by adding a polarity to the edges of an existing graph, and this concept of signed graphs has recently been integrated with other graph theory ideas like minors and coloring. By examining the notion of Extended Double Covers (EDC), we can now explore a potential bound on signed graph homomorphisms, similar to the recent work by Kostochka and Thomassé on graph minor theory and the Four Color Theorem. Specifically, we are looking for a double cover of a signed graph to understand its homomorphism bounds, and in doing so, we can derive conclusions about the relationship between the homomorphism to a graph double cover and the original graph cover.

For a class of quadratic Hamiltonians, a transformation of Weyl-Wigner symbols through a canonical equilibrium state results in a diagonal representation, with the eigenvalues being uniform constants, independent of phase space variables.

The notion of negative absolute temperature has been substantiated, no longer being merely a theoretical concept. Within this report, statistical mechanics and thermodynamics formalism are combined to illustrate negative temperature through both mathematical and graphical means, specifically in the context of a two-level system. We contend that the simplicity of these calculations can offer undergraduates a clear, tangible understanding of the concept of negative absolute temperature.

Let G be an abelian group and A a nonempty subset of G, with elements indexed as $a_0, a_1,..., a_{k-1}$. For any positive integer h less than or equal to k, we can calculate a restricted signed sumset denoted as $h\hat{}_{\underline{+}}A$, which comprises sums of $a_i$ with weights from {-1,0,1}. The goal of this article is to solve the minimum value of $|h\hat{}_{\underline{+}}A|$, where $|A|$, when A is a set of integers, and investigate the underlying structure of A to achieve this minimum value. Additionally, some open questions related to $h\hat{}_{\underline{+}}A$ are proposed in this article.

Characterizing colorectal polyps histopathologically is crucial to personalize patient treatment and follow-up, ultimately reducing the risk of undetected invasive carcinomas. The process of polyp characterization involves examining tissue samples for malignancy and dysplasia using histological analysis. Recent advancements in deep learning have significantly improved medical pattern recognition accuracy; however, training these models necessitates vast collections of annotated medical images. In this context, we've developed UniToPatho, an extensive dataset consisting of 9536 annotated H&E stained patches derived from 292 whole-slide images, designed for deep learning-based classification and grading of colorectal polyps and adenomas. This dataset serves as a resource for researchers tackling the complex task of automating colorectal polyp characterization.

A novel numerical approach has been introduced for solving time-harmonic acoustic scattering issues, primarily centered around analyzing the impact of smoothly varying material inhomogeneities on plane waves. This method's efficiency is optimal for high-frequency scenarios and is adaptable across any given frequency. Its key components are an adaptive finite element technique, tailored to scattering problems, and the application of asymptotic approximations to rapidly oscillating solutions. When the wavenumber is substantial, adaptive computations are streamlined by utilizing a highly accurate asymptotic method as an initial guess in iterative solution processes for the discretized wave equations. Research indicates that only a relatively small proportion of global degrees of freedom are needed to achieve an accurate solution, as the amplitude of the scattering amplitude's oscillations diminishes with increasing wavenumber. Moreover, the number of adaptive steps required for optimizing the global mesh condition remains unaffected by higher wavenumbers. These YG-scaled amplitude components play a crucial computational role, significantly reducing the overall efficiency in computational time and cost.

We analyzed the isotopic composition of hydrogen and water content in pyroxene minerals from recent chondrite falls in Benenitra (2018) and Chelyabinsk (2013), as well as three older chondrite falls in Japan. In addition, we compared these findings with laboratory simulations of water on dust aggregates during the growth of early planetesimals. To assess accuracy, we calibrated our instruments using pyroxene samples with known hydrogen isotopic compositions. The benonotonic water extraction technique revealed varying levels of incorporated hydrogen and water in the pyroxene minerals from Benenitra to Chelyabinsk, exhibiting distinct characteristics in quantity and isotopic composition. Based on D/H ratios, pyroxene samples from Benenitra, Chelyabinsk, and Naoetsu can be categorized into two groups sharing similar D/H ratios but differing in water content. According to our lab experiments, high D/H ratios can result from the accretion of water-rich planetesimals in a cold environment, which is indicative of ice-covered dust aggregates with high surface D/H ratios. Water was also found within the pyroxene minerals from Benenitra and Chelyabinsk, which is inconsistent with the water evaporation at temperatures above 150 K. Thus, our research is indicative of the wet process in the formation of planetesimals in the inner solar system.

Using the algebraic Bethe-ansatz method, we find exact expressions for scalar products and form factors of higher-spin XXZ chains. This applies to any spin values and mixtures thereof. We verify the affine quantum-group symmetry, $U_q(\hat{sl_2})$, for the XXZ chain's monodromy matrix, enabling exact derivation. Specifically, we find precision 2 and form operator expressions for spin-1/2 chains and outline a general approach. These expressions are validated by their affine quantum-group symmetry. Additionally, we provide detailed calculations for spin-1/2 and spin-1 chains, confirming the formation operator expressions against known results. These results contribute to understanding correlation functions in spin chains through the use of the Lindner identity.

Speech-to-text translation involves converting spoken language into written language across different tongues. Conventional two-stage approaches using speech recognition and machine translation have inherent flaws, primarily stemming from the use of suboptimal reference transcripts. This study introduces a zero-shot method leveraging spoken language into written language using multi-lingual models pre-trained on text-based data. Notably, our experiments reveal that our approach outperforms the industry-standard two-stage approach by a significant margin when utilizing datasets comprising diverse accents.

We assess the applicability of three different methods for calculating electromagnetic multipoles: Cartesian primitive multipoles, irreducible multipoles and spherical multipoles. Our findings suggest that the spherical multipoles provide the most accurate description of electromagnetic scattering behavior, as demonstrated with an example of an amorphous silicon sphere. These multipoles are utilized to model the optical force exerted on particles composed of semiconductors, dielectrics, and metals over a broad range of wavelengths spanning from the dipolar regime down to the Mie regime.

This study introduces two categories of elements within the algebra U(y_1, y_2), each associated with a Young diagram, and establishes a connection to the algebra s_lambda~. A specific linear transformation is defined that maps s_delta~ to a combination of s_mu~, and the matrix representing this transformation comprises entries that are products of shifted factorials. This product algebra u(y_1, y_2) is shown to be isomorphic to the algebra of quantum shifted symmetric functions through the assignment of a set of generators. Furthermore, s_lambda~ is identified as a quotient of the algebra of dual quantum shifted symmetric functions, and this relationship enables an expression of the immanant function using quantum shifted symmetric functions.

Within the simplest scoto-seesaw model, we examine the consistency between the electroweak symmetry breaking, neutrino characteristics, and dark matter behavior. By integrating the minimal dark sector into the simplest Scoto-Seesaw (SS) framework, we establish the interconnections among neutrino mass magnitude, dark matter mass density, and neutrinoless double beta decay rates. Our analysis incorporates limits from direct dark matter detection experiments, thermal dark matter abundance calculations, and theoretical constraints on the stability of the vacuum. Notably, we utilize a potential formula considering third-order perturbations to assess the vacuum stability. Our findings reveal that a substantial parameter range exists where the model is consistent, although it is restricted to specific values within the neutrino mixing matrix phase angle.

We employ a simplified model to investigate how the electron interactions affect the combined states of $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ orbitals in oxides containing 4d and 5d transition metals. Our study reveals that electron interactions cause a combined spectrum with distinct regions where only $t_{2g}$ or $e_g$ electrons exist, plus a central region where the two types of electrons are mixed. The size of this mixed region is crucial, as it can have a significant impact on the material's properties, especially in cerium-based compounds. Our theoretical analysis is supported by actual X-ray absorption spectroscopy data for examples such as SrIrO$_3$, BaRPtO$_4$, and LaSr$_2$CeCu$_6$O$_{19}$.

This research examines how relative quantum cohomology evolves under certain transformations of algebraic varieties. Specifically, when a variety transforms into another through a degeneration that maintains the underlying structure, we establish the corresponding relationship between their relative twisted I-functions. Furthermore, this relative relationship is applied to demonstrate the connection between the relative -pair and the 3-fold Atiyah flop.

Using generative adversarial networks, a novel application in disease-aware image editing has emerged, which could revolutionize AI usage in the healthcare field. In this research, a concept for GAN-based medical imaging enhancement is demonstrated. Though GAN-based techniques excel at natural image creation and manipulation, their potential in medicine remains largely unexplored. Our research utilized the CheXpert dataset to train a StyleGAN that effectively produces authentic chest X-rays. By incorporating an encoder from the Cyclic Reverse Generator framework, we successfully developed an inverse mapping system to recreate synthetic X-rays accurately and reconstruct organs on real X-rays. By fine-tuning latent codes, we successfully transplanted a cardiac enlargement condition onto normal chest X-rays. Our research was showcased at the Medical Imaging meets NeurIPS Workshop 2020, a satellite event of the 34th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems held in Vancouver, Canada.

ViDaExpert is an application for multidimensional data visualization and
advanced analysis. It is capable of handling object-feature tables that include
numerical values and text-based labels for objects and features. The tool
encompasses several statistical techniques such as weighted PCA, elastic maps,
linear discriminant analysis, and decision tree construction, in addition to
K-Means clustering and multilinear regression. With customizable visualizations
and an interactive 3D viewer, ViDaExpert enables the creation of 3D scenes
from data and facilitates rapid, in-depth analysis of data, encompassing
multistage processing and visual report generation.

Evaluating Newtonian potentials over complex two-dimensional regions is essential in various biomedical and geological applications, as well as in electrostatics and fluid dynamics. In three-dimensional space, a novel boundary reduction technique has been developed for accelerating potential calculations. This paper introduces its two-dimensional counterpart and demonstrates its effectiveness through comparative performance tests and visualisation examples. Our implementation uses open-source software, making the algorithm easily replicable for users.
